title: Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
summary: Deserialization of untrusted data in the report-processing code of Puppet, as used by Puppet Server, in the affected releases, allows a client that holds any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as its service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type via PUT request. Where the certificate authority autosigns requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain such a certificate.

title: Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability
summary:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

title: PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability
summary: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

title: Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability
summary: An unauthenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerability was found in the survey passthrough routing and Data Import processing logic, in which a malicious user could potentially exploit it by manipulating HTTP requests to access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and by supplying a crafted file-path/stream parameter during import handling. If successfully exploited, this could allow the attacker to remotely execute arbitrary code on the REDCap server. The attacker does not have to be authenticated in order to exploit this, but exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash. This vulnerability exists in REDCap 13.3.0 and higher.

title: PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability
summary: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

title: cf-manager is an all-in-one dashboard for managing multiple Cloudflare accounts and services.
summary: cf-manager is an all-in-one dashboard for managing multiple Cloudflare accounts and services. Prior to 1.1.2, worker/src/routes/workers.ts uses bare fetch(url) calls to retrieve user-supplied URLs and deploys the returned content as a Worker script using stored Cloudflare credentials. The multipart and JSON branches of POST /api/:accountId/workers and POST /api/batch-deploy accept URLs without protocol, destination, redirect, content-type, or response-size validation. An attacker with deployment API access, or unauthenticated access when API_SECRET is not configured, can make cf-manager access internal resources or fetch attacker-controlled JavaScript and execute it in the victim Cloudflare Workers account. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.2.

title: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS).
summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the backup prefix field is only checked for a nonempty value, and normalizeS3Path preserves shell metacharacters before the prefix is interpolated into rclone upload and retention-cleanup command strings. An authenticated organization member with backup permission for a service can execute arbitrary commands as root on the Dokploy host or configured remote server when a PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, libSQL, Compose, or web-server backup runs manually, on schedule, or performs retention cleanup. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

title: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS).
summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the Nixpacks publishDirectory build setting accepts shell metacharacters and is interpolated into a docker cp command executed through child_process.exec. An authenticated user with access to an application can execute arbitrary commands on the Dokploy host when triggering a Nixpacks deployment, leading to host compromise through the privileged Docker environment. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

title: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS).
summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, mount.deleteFileMount passes a path containing the user-controlled filePath to the local removeFileOrDirectory helper, which interpolates it unquoted into rm -rf, while the remote branch is quoted. An authenticated member with file-mount create and delete permissions can execute arbitrary commands in the host context immediately when deleting a local file mount, without requiring a running container. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

title: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS).
summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). From 0.29.13 until 0.31.0, the Docker terminal, container-log, and monitoring WebSocket handlers accept a caller-controlled serviceId as authorization but do not consistently bind the requested containerId or appName to that service. A member with read access to any service can consequently target unrelated containers, obtain a root shell in the Dokploy panel container, read other tenants' logs and statistics, and use the mounted Docker socket to compromise the host. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.

title: A vulnerability has been found in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6.
summary: A vulnerability has been found in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6. This vulnerability affects the function doWebBackup of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi of the component Backup Handler. Such manipulation of the argument path/value leads to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is able to resolve this issue. The affected component should be upgraded. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

title: A vulnerability was detected in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6.

The manipulation of the argument usefile results in stack-based buffer overflow. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 can resolve this issue. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

title: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS).
summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, the database password validation used by the MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, and Redis change-password procedures permits backticks, and the procedures interpolate attacker-controlled passwords into Bash command strings. An authenticated user who can update a database password can trigger command substitution before the database command runs, resulting in arbitrary operating-system command execution with the Dokploy process privileges, which are typically root. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

title: A weakness has been identified in DrayTek Vigor2960 up to 1.5.1.6.

Executing a manipulation of the argument filename can lead to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 is able to address this issue. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

title: ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application.
summary: ZoneMinder is a free, open source closed-circuit television software application. Prior to 1.38.4, any authenticated user can use the /api/configs/edit/{name}.json endpoint to modify protected configuration settings because ConfigsController::edit() does not enforce the System=Edit authorization requirement and its system-variable protection is ineffective. An attacker can set ZM_PATH_FFMPEG to a command-bearing value and trigger an exec() sink in web/views/image.php or web/includes/Event.php by requesting frame extraction. This permits arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the web server user and can expose private camera feeds, recordings, and database data or establish persistence. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.4.

title: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and incl...
summary: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.11 via the save_single_batch_file function. This is due to a PHP type-juggling authentication bypass via loose != comparison with no is_string() guard, combined with unsanitized base64-decoded path construction in save_single_batch_file() lacking any directory traversal containment. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to execute code on the server. Exploitation requires that the site owner has completed the plugin's initial setup so that the site_type and prod_key_random_id options are non-empty, though any non-empty secret value is bypassable via the type-juggling flaw.

title: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms.
summary: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms uses a public hard-coded fallback JWT signing secret from server/config/auth.config.js when ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET is unset. An unauthenticated attacker can sign a self-contained token with privileged claims because server/src/auth/auth_jwt.js verifies the signature without reloading the user from the database, and server/src/lib/middleware.js trusts the token's roles and options for authorization. A forged token can therefore be accepted as an administrator session, resulting in authentication bypass and full privileged API access. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.1.

title: Dialoqbase is an application for creating chatbots.
summary: Dialoqbase is an application for creating chatbots. title: The Masteriyo LMS – LMS Course Builder, Quizzes & Certificates plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up ...
summary: The Masteriyo LMS – LMS Course Builder, Quizzes & Certificates plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 3.5.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the course importer. The set_post_metas() method  calls maybe_unserialize() on attacker-controlled postmeta string values parsed from the uploaded JSON import file. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP Objects. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that the site has enable_instructor_registration=true AND enable_guest_checkout=true AND at least one purchasable course exists. Install.php sets enable_instructor_registration=false on fresh installs, so this is a non-default configuration. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

title: When BIG-IP APM is provisioned and a per-request policy that includes the Client Information agent and Endpoint Security agents is applie...
summary:
When BIG-IP APM is provisioned and a per-request policy that includes the Client Information agent and Endpoint Security agents is applied to a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE).

Impact:

Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

title: The Trust Payments Gateway for WooCommerce (JavaScript Library) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versio...
summary: The Trust Payments Gateway for WooCommerce (JavaScript Library) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.8. The vulnerability exists because the `new_customer_account()` function stores the raw return value of `wp_create_user()` — including a `WP_Error` object returned on username collision — into the order's `tp_userid` post meta before the `is_wp_error()` guard is evaluated; the `add_customer_details_to_thankyou_page()` callback subsequently reads that meta and casts it with `(int)`, causing PHP to coerce any object to integer `1`, after which `wp_set_current_user(1)` and `wp_set_auth_cookie(1)` are called unconditionally. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as WordPress user ID 1 — the bootstrap site administrator or, on multisite, a network super-admin — by supplying the `new_username` parameter matching any existing login during checkout and visiting the resulting thank-you page. Exploitation requires the Trust Payments gateway to be active and the attacker to complete a paid order on their own account; the ID 1 administrator username is additionally enumerable via standard WordPress user enumeration techniques.

title: The Unzer Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and inc...
summary: The Unzer Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1. The vulnerability exists because the Google Pay Express Checkout endpoint (`/?wc-api=google_pay_express`), handled by `startCheckoutDataWithNormalizedCustomerData`, accepts an attacker-controlled `paymentData.email` value and passes it to `createOrGetGuestCustomer()`, which resolves the submitted email to any existing WordPress user via `get_user_by('email', ...)` and then calls `wp_set_current_user()` and `wp_set_auth_cookie()` for the resolved user ID without verifying ownership of the email address, a password, a nonce, an authentication token, or any proof of payment from the payment provider. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any existing WordPress user — including administrators — by submitting that user's known email address, receiving valid `wordpress_logged_in_*` session cookies for the targeted account and achieving full site takeover. The endpoint is entirely unprotected with no capability check, nonce validation, or payment-provider signature verification applied, and administrator email addresses are frequently discoverable via the WordPress REST API user enumeration endpoint (`/wp-json/wp/v2/users`), author archive pages, Gravatar lookups, or site contact footers.

title: Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK.
summary:
Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK. The TCP client method CreatePersonalAccessToken wrote the 32-bit expiry into the upper half of the 64-bit expiry field that the server reads. The server read a nonzero expiry as 2^32 times the requested value. A token created through the Go TCP client therefore stayed valid about four billion times longer than the caller asked for.

This issue affects Apache Iggy Go SDK: from 0.5.0 before 0.10.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Tokens that an earlier version created keep their long expiry on the server. Delete those tokens and create new ones.

title: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames.
summary: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.

title: Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport.
summary:
Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

title:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** 



Improper Authentication in Apache SeaTunnel Web 1.0.2 allows a user whose account has been disabled t...
summary:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** 



Improper Authentication in Apache SeaTunnel Web 1.0.2 allows a user whose account has been disabled to authenticate with valid credentials and obtain a new login token. The login query does not check the account status, so disabling an account does not prevent new logins or access to protected APIs using the newly issued token. This issue requires valid credentials for the disabled account; it is not a credential-free authentication bypass.



Apache SeaTunnel Web is no longer maintained. The affected 1.0.2 release does not contain the account-status check added to the main branch in pull request #264. There is no maintained fixed release. Users should discontinue use of this unsupported component.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

title: IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data ...
summary:
IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source.

The rewrite copies the module's source down to the built-in list's heredoc and appends each fetched line below it. Nothing checks that a line looks like a domain. A line that is not a comment loses only what follows a `//` and its trailing whitespace, so a line reading END_BUILTIN_DATA is appended as it stands and ends the data block in the rewritten file. Every fetched line after it is Perl.

Arbitrary Perl runs in every process that loads IO::Socket::SSL, which loads this module unconditionally, until the file is reinstalled. The attacker must control the fetched list, through the cleartext default URL or a caller-supplied one, and the updater must run with write access to the installed module.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()

client_has_openowners...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()

client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids
without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under
cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched
creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner.

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in client_has_state+0x10a/0x140
  fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:3718 client_has_openowners()
  nfsd4_exchange_id
  nfsd4_proc_compound
  nfsd_dispatch
  svc_process

Take clp->cl_lock while client_has_openowners() walks the openowner
list.

summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: reject mdsmaps that claim more than CEPH_MAX_MDS ranks

check_new_map() sizes its export-target bitmap from CEPH_MAX_MDS but walks
it with newmap->possible_max_rank, which comes straight off the wire:
ceph_mdsmap_decode() sets it to max(m_num_active_mds, m_max_mds), then
overwrites it with the size of the "in" set.  Neither is bounded by
CEPH_MAX_MDS, only by m_info allocating, so a monitor announcing more ranks
than the bitmap holds makes test_bit() read past the end of targets[].  The
clear_bit() loop above indexes the same bitmap, though it is additionally
bounded by mdsc->max_sessions.  The map arrives on the monitor connection,
which is unauthenticated in legacy msgr mode.

CEPH_MAX_MDS is a protocol constant from src/mds/mdstypes.h, and the
reserved inode ranges in super.h are laid out one rank apart over that
span, so a map claiming more ranks is corrupt.  Reject it where the rank
space is established rather than letting the count reach check_new_map().

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check

ceph_upda...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fix integer overflow in the snap trace bounds check

ceph_update_snap_trace() bounds the two encoded snapid arrays that follow a
struct ceph_mds_snap_realm with sizeof(u64) * (num_snaps +
num_prior_parent_snaps).  Both counts come straight off the wire as __le32,
so the addition is evaluated in unsigned int and wraps before sizeof(u64)
promotes it to size_t: an MDS sending num_snaps = 1 and
num_prior_parent_snaps = 0xffffffff makes the sum zero and the check
degenerates to ceph_decode_need(&p, e, 0, bad), which always passes.
dup_array() then reads num_snaps * 8 bytes past the end of the message
front, which ceph_msg_new2() allocates at exactly front_len bytes.  An
unsolicited CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_SNAP reaches this from a malicious or
compromised MDS with no client-side action, as do the snaptraces carried in
an MDS reply and in a cap import.

Compute the length with size_add()/size_mul() so it saturates at SIZE_MAX
instead of wrapping, in the style fs/ceph/mdsmap.c already uses for
num_export_targets.

title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Camel.
summary:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Camel.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The camel-hazelcast component applies a default Hazelcast JavaSerializationFilterConfig to the instances it creates from its own configuration, a protection introduced by CVE-2026-43865. That change did not reach two of the configuration paths Camel builds itself, so those paths continued to create Hazelcast instances whose Java deserialization is unrestricted. ReplicatedHazelcastAggregationRepository extends HazelcastAggregationRepository but overrides doStart() without calling super.doStart(), keeping its own copy of the bootstrap block, and therefore never received the filter: a route using it without supplying a hazelcastInstance starts a Hazelcast member that deserializes values read from the backing ReplicatedMap with no class restriction. HazelcastDefaultComponent#getOrCreateHzClientInstance() builds its own ClientConfig when hazelcastMode=client is selected and neither a referenced ClientConfig nor hazelcastConfigUri is supplied, and likewise applied no filter, so client-mode endpoints behaved differently from node-mode endpoints for an otherwise identical configuration. In both cases an attacker able to publish into the Hazelcast cluster that the affected instance is attached to can cause a serialized Java object of their choosing to be deserialized inside Hazelcast's own serialization layer, before Camel processes the exchange, resulting in remote code execution. Hazelcast clusters have neither authentication nor TLS enabled by default. Selecting client mode is a topology choice rather than a security option, so neither path required the deployment to opt in to unsafe behaviour.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.1. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.14.x releases stream and earlier reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on those lines must move to a supported release. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, supply an explicit Hazelcast configuration carrying a JavaSerializationFilterConfig, or inject a pre-built HazelcastInstance, since a user-supplied configuration is never overwritten by Camel. Alternatively set the JVM-wide filter -Djdk.serialFilter=!java.net.;java.;javax.;org.apache.camel.;!* and enable Hazelcast cluster authentication and TLS to restrict who can reach the cluster.

title: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support.
summary: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support. Incomplete validation of shell metacharacters allows an authenticated user who owns a volume on an affected backend to supply crafted connection information and inject additional commands into the storage array's management interface. Commands execute with the privileges of Cinder's configured backend account. This can disclose storage configuration information and, where that account has administrative permissions, could allow changes that affect the integrity or availability of other tenants' storage.

title: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software.
summary: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 2.5, the filename parameter accepted by POST /qsl/addQsoToQsl in application/controllers/Qsl.php addQsoToQsl() is stored without rejecting directory separators or relative path components, and POST /qsl/delete reaches application/models/Qsl_model.php deleteQsl(), which passes the planted qsl_images filename to unlink(). A standard authenticated user can associate the malicious filename with the user's own QSO, satisfy the ownership check, escape the per-user QSL image directory, and delete files writable by the PHP worker. Deleting configuration or operational files can cause denial of service, while deleting installer gate files can reopen the unauthenticated installer and enable application identity takeover through attacker-controlled database configuration. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.

title: LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in its e-mail-based Helpdesk ticket intake.
summary:
LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in its e-mail-based Helpdesk ticket intake. The mail parser does not reject Apache .htaccess configuration files or PHP-executable files when saving ticket attachments. A remote unauthenticated attacker can e-mail a Helpdesk ticket with such an attachment; in the default configuration, anyone can request the uploaded file's URL which executes attacker-supplied code with the privileges of the web server process. No operator interaction or LMS client session is required.


The issue was fixed in commit d5059b1.

title: A bug in the Airlock Gateway (8.5.2 and earlier, and 8.6.0)  allows attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response to exploit the Smart F...
summary:
A bug in the Airlock Gateway (8.5.2 and earlier, and 8.6.0)  allows attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response to exploit the Smart Form Protection feature, possibly leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or Remote Code Execution (RCE) attack against the Airlock Gateway. The issue has been fixed in Airlock Gateway version 8.5.3 and 8.6.1.

For an attack to be executable, the Airlock Gateway needs to have 'Smart Form Protection' (or the corresponding expert settings) enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references. The buffer overflow then happens during the parsing of that HTML response. Such a response can come either from a malicious or compromised backend, or from an otherwise trusted backend that returns attacker-supplied HTML, e.g. an application that stores and serves plain user-provided HTML files.

Successfully exploiting the vulnerability can enable an attacker to perform a DoS attack or, in the worst case, an RCE attack against the Airlock Gateway in front of the affected backend. Compromising the functionality of the Airlock Gateway could in this way also affect the availability and protection of other well-intentioned backends deployed behind the same Gateway.

title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could use an empty clustering shared sec...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could use an empty clustering shared secret to read and modify clustering configuration through the cluster configuration Representational State Transfer (REST) API endpoint on a standalone instance. This could expose clustering configuration, persist attacker-controlled clustering settings, and disrupt clustering operations.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts the empty clustering shared secret as a shared-authentication candidate on a standalone instance when clustering is turned off.

title: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software.
summary: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 2.5, the callsign parameter accepted by POST /oqrs/search_log in application/controllers/Oqrs.php search_log() reaches application/models/Oqrs_model.php search_log(), where it is concatenated directly into a raw SQL WHERE clause without parameter binding. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use UNION-based SQL injection to read arbitrary application database records, including account data, password hashes, API keys, station credentials, reset tokens, QSO data, and station metadata. Disclosure of password reset tokens can be combined with the forgot_password workflow to take over accounts, including administrator accounts. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.

title: Bazarr is a companion application to Sonarr and Radarr.
summary: Bazarr is a companion application to Sonarr and Radarr. Prior to 1.6.3-beta.11, the /api/subtitles/subtitles-info handler uses SubtitleNameContents.get() in subtitles_contents.py and reads the caller-supplied subtitlePath after checking only its subtitle extension; because the resolved path is not confined to files indexed by Bazarr, traversal can read files outside the media library. The /api/subtitles/subtitles handler in subtitles.py passes caller-supplied path and reference to sync and translation without per-path authorization, allowing an out-of-library reference file to be read and output to overwrite a file outside the media library. The authenticate decorator gates both endpoints when API authentication is enabled, while auth = None allows access without credentials. Both paths can affect only files that the Bazarr process can read or write. This issue is fixed in version 1.6.3-beta.11.

title: LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to privilege escalation in the lmsd daemon.
summary:
LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to privilege escalation in the lmsd daemon. The daemon loads the libraries listed in the LMS database without checking that they come from a trusted location. An attacker with access to the web server process or with write access to the LMS database can register a malicious library and trigger a configuration reload, causing lmsd to load and execute it. Because the example systemd unit does not set a separate user, lmsd runs as root, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges.
This issue was fixed in commit 89dd3f7. The lmsd component was removed. For existing installations that use lmsd, the recommended solution is to disable and remove this component.

title: Vulnerability in the Oracle WebLogic Server product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Core).
summary: Vulnerability in the Oracle WebLogic Server product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Core).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0, 14.1.2.0.0 and  15.1.1.0.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data and unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of Oracle WebLogic Server. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 9.4 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:H).

title: The installer (first installation wizard) could be re-enabled on an already configured instance by placing a file whose name starts with ...
summary:
The installer (first installation wizard) could be re-enabled on an already configured instance by placing a file whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL in the public web root or the project root. The installer then became accessible without authentication, allowing for example to change the database connection and to create a new administrator and system maintainer account, which leads to remote code execution. As demonstrated in TYPO3-CORE-SA-2026-026, such a file could be created by an authenticated, low-privileged backend user without any further permissions. Other ways of creating files in the web root, as well as leftover or restored marker files, could be abused in the same way.

With the fixed versions, the installer can no longer be re-enabled on an already configured instance by a marker file. A new internal setting $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SYS']['isInstalling'] is stored in the system configuration and is only enabled while a new installation is running. Additionally, only the exact file names FIRST_INSTALL and FIRST_INSTALL.txt are accepted as marker files.

title: CubeSandbox is an instant, concurrent, secure, and lightweight sandbox for AI agents.
summary: CubeSandbox is an instant, concurrent, secure, and lightweight sandbox for AI agents. Prior to 0.5.1, any authenticated tenant permitted to call POST /sandboxes can supply metadata["host-mount"] with an arbitrary existing host path because the control plane performs no authorization check or allowed-prefix validation for the path. injectHostDirMounts forwards the path to prepareHostDirVolume, where Cubelet uses mount --rbind through the function to perform a recursive bind mount as root and exposes the host subtree to the tenant's MicroVM through virtio-fs, read-write by default. This allows host-root file access and modification, host code execution, access to the container runtime, and compromise of co-resident tenants without a kernel or virtual-machine-monitor flaw. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.1.

title: WatchGuard Dimension records unredacted session identifiers for logged-in users in its web UI diagnostic log.
summary:
WatchGuard Dimension records unredacted session identifiers for logged-in users in its web UI diagnostic log. A low-privileged Dimension Administrator can retrieve this log and extract a Super Administrator's session token while that administrator is logged in, enabling account takeover.

This vulnerability is a secondary unmitigated attack path for CVE-2026-78174.

title: WatchGuard Dimension returns unredacted session identifiers for logged-in users in a management API response.
summary: WatchGuard Dimension returns unredacted session identifiers for logged-in users in a management API response. A low-privileged Dimension Administrator can retrieve the active session IDs of other administrators, including Super Administrators, while they are logged in, enabling account takeover.

summary:
The preview mode of the OPC (OnPage Composer) page
builder of JTL-Shop is activated by a request parameter alone and
renders page data supplied in the request without checking for an authenticated
backend session with the corresponding permission. Several portlet properties
are output without output encoding. An unauthenticated remote attacker
can thereby cause script code to be executed in the browser of a
visitor or administrator who opens a crafted link; in the case of an
administrator, actions can be performed with the administrator's privileges. Third-party
plugins whose portlets evaluate property values as templates can
additionally be made to execute template code through the same entry point. This is
a separate flaw in such plugins and does not affect the portlets of JTL-Shop itself.

title: Sprout Track is a self-hosted baby tracking application.
summary: Sprout Track is a self-hosted baby tracking application. Prior to 1.3.5, Sprout Track uses a publicly known hardcoded signing secret when JWT_SECRET is unset, and standard setup does not generate a unique secret. On a network-reachable affected deployment, an unauthenticated attacker can sign JWTs with arbitrary claims, including system-administrator claims, to access administrative functionality and read or modify family, child activity, account, and email data. Deployments with a strong unique JWT_SECRET are not affected. Managed and hosted instances were reported remediated. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.5.

summary:
The visitor tracking of JTL-Shop automatically
registers unknown crawler user agents without filtering the value, and the stored
value is rendered without output encoding on several pages of the
administration backend (search engine statistics, crawler dashboard widget, crawler
edit form, sitemap export download list and campaign details). An
unauthenticated remote attacker can store script code with a single request. The code is
executed in the browser session of an administrator who opens one of these
pages, allowing actions to be performed with the administrator's privileges.

title: The Comelit 1456B Multi-User Gateway, in firmware versions up to and including 2.10.0, is configured with static default passwords for mu...
summary: The Comelit 1456B Multi-User Gateway, in firmware versions up to and including 2.10.0, is configured with static default passwords for multiple privileged roles. None of these passwords are required to be changed during initial configuration, and they remain at their default values unless the administrator changes them manually. An attacker with network access to the device can authenticate using these default credentials and gain administrative control.

title: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics.
summary: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/database/import handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/database.py accepts a ZIP archive and moves an included database file to DATABASE_PATH while also replacing IMAGE_PATH content. An attacker can supply a database containing an attacker-controlled users table and administrative account, then authenticate as that account; invalid replacement data can also destroy application data or availability. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

title: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics.
summary: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/images/manga/save handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/image.py accepts a client-controlled filename and joins it to IMAGE_SAVE_PATH without confining the result. Traversal sequences can escape the image directory and overwrite process-writable files, including DATABASE_PATH for the live SQLite database, while the client-supplied image content type does not validate the uploaded bytes. An attacker can replace the database to plant an administrative user and can overwrite other writable files, causing full application compromise and availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

title: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implem...
summary: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. In 1.11.2 and earlier, rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c uses one session-wide autoadj_tally to learn RTP sources that differ from the address negotiated in SDP. An unauthenticated remote attacker who sends plaintext RTP during call setup can make packets from one or more non-advertised sources reach the threshold before the legitimate endpoint, causing FreeSWITCH to adopt the source of the threshold-crossing packet as the media peer. The attacker can then receive call audio, inject media, and deny media to the legitimate endpoint without being on the media path. FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 adds two opt-in controls, but both default to zero and the release remains affected unless both are configured before RTP session creation. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.11.2.

title: Eclipse Zenoh's zenoh-pico implementation, versions 0.7.2-rc up to but excluding 1.10.2, does not validate the Zenoh identifier (ZID) len...
summary:
Eclipse Zenoh's zenoh-pico implementation, versions 0.7.2-rc up to but excluding 1.10.2, does not validate the Zenoh identifier (ZID) length when deserializing timestamps. An attacker-controlled length greater than 16 causes an out-of-bounds write to a fixed 16-byte identifier buffer and causes the subsequent zero-fill operation to receive a negative length converted to a large unsigned size. Truncated timestamp inputs can also cause out-of-bounds reads or assertion failures. A remote attacker able to deliver crafted timestamp-bearing Zenoh messages through an accepted transport can cause memory corruption and denial of service, with potential remote code execution in builds lacking appropriate binary protections. This issue is fixed in version 1.10.2.



Depending on the release and message-decoding path, the unchecked timestamp identifier length causes a heap-based or stack-based buffer overflow. Ordinary-frame network message decoding moved from heap-backed storage to stack-local storage in version 1.5.0. Earlier affected releases already contained stack-based decoding paths, including reassembled fragmented messages.

title: Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data vulnerability in the Sign in with Apple strategy in pow-auth Assent allows an u...
summary:
Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data vulnerability in the Sign in with Apple strategy in pow-auth Assent allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to impersonate another user via the user parameter of the authorization callback.

Apple posts the user's name to the callback endpoint in a user form parameter that the browser submits and the client controls. Assent.Strategy.Apple.callback/2 in lib/assent/strategies/apple.ex decodes that parameter, and fetch_user/2 merges it over the claims of the verified ID token, so the unverified map wins. An attacker who completes a Sign in with Apple login with their own Apple ID and edits the user parameter can replace sub, email, and any other claim. Applications that look up, link, or authorize accounts by the returned subject or email then act on the attacker's values.

This issue affects assent: from 0.1.25 before 0.3.2.

title: Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution.
summary:
Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution.

In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. A diagnostic raised early in the first request of a worker, such as the max_input_vars warning, then accesses the freed cache. On such a deployment an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI workers with a crafted request. Arbitrary code execution may be possible and has been demonstrated with known memory addresses.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title: Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown.
summary:
Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown.

The session extension records the filename of the executing script when a session starts. If a fatal error occurs in an application callback while the session variables are destroyed at shutdown, such as stream_close() of a user-defined stream wrapper, the pointer is retained after the request memory is freed, and a later request handled by the same worker can free the stale string. An attacker who can trigger such a failing cleanup may crash the worker or corrupt memory; code execution has not been demonstrated. This requires the filename to be allocated in request memory, for example when the script is not cached by OPcache.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title: Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution.
summary:
Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution.

When collecting the arguments of a method call handled by __call() or __callStatic() for a backtrace, PHP can read stale values that may refer to freed memory. If a fatal error such as exceeding memory_limit occurs while an application enters such a call, with fatal_error_backtraces enabled (the default) and zend.exception_ignore_args disabled, a remote attacker who controls enough request data to influence memory allocation may cause memory corruption, crash the PHP worker or, with knowledge of memory addresses, execute arbitrary code. php.ini-production enables zend.exception_ignore_args, which prevents this.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title: PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.
summary:
PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title: Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown.
summary:
Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown.

A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repopulate the stored fatal error backtrace after the executor has been cleaned up. The request memory is then freed, and a diagnostic emitted before executor initialization in a later request handled by the same PHP-FPM or mod_php worker can access the stale backtrace. The shutdown error requires per-path configuration of max_memory_limit, or of zlib.output_compression together with output_handler (which .user.ini can also set). The early diagnostic requires Apache per-directory configuration or, for PHP-FPM, a PHP_VALUE or PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameter sent by the front end. This can cause memory corruption and worker crashes, and may allow remote code execution.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title: Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.
summary:
Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title: Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.
summary:
Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.

Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title: CAST Imaging is vulnerable to authentication bypass in the TenantFilter class.
summary:
CAST Imaging is vulnerable to authentication bypass in the TenantFilter class. The TenantFilter processes the X-ISSUER-LOCATION HTTP header and dynamically registers an OpenID Connect issuer based on its value. An unauthenticated remote attacker can register a malicious identity provider, create users matching existing administrative usernames, and obtain valid JWTs which will be accepted by the application. This results in complete authentication bypass and privilege escalation to administrative access.




The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

title: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker.

Requests to selected invalid or redirecting paths also generate a log entry for each request, allowing network traffic to expand logs and exhaust constrained storage such as an SD card, while other request forms consume CPU without producing a corresponding request log. title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could run arbitrary Search Proce...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches through RapidDiag task collection as an authenticated user. With this access, the user could read or modify data and configuration available to that authenticated user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts an empty shared secret when it authenticates RapidDiag task-collection requests.
For more information see Using RapidDiag (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/troubleshoot/9.3/contact-splunk-support/using-rapiddiag) in the Splunk documentation.

title: Fabio is an HTTP(S) and TCP router for deploying applications managed by consul.
summary: Fabio is an HTTP(S) and TCP router for deploying applications managed by consul. Prior to 1.7.3, route/table.go selects targets using raw req.URL.Path, while proxy/http_proxy.go applies per-route ACL and basic-auth checks to the selected target and forwards the raw path to the origin. Dot-segment, encoded-dot, or repeated-slash variants can fall through to a less restrictive route that reaches the same backend; the backend then normalizes the path and serves the protected resource without the configured access controls. A less restrictive fallback route must reach the same backend; without one, the request returns 404. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.3.

title: In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject n...
summary: In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (`global.jwtOnly: false`, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (`ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false`) or, when using the Helm chart, configure `global.jwtOnly: true`.

title: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal.
summary: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to Open OnDemand 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, and prior to ood-ansible 4.2.1, the portal generator defaults OIDCCryptoPassphrase to SHA1(servername), and the templates/ood_portal.yml.j2 role checks a different variable from the documented passphrase setting. Administrators who set ood_oidc_crypto_passphrase can therefore believe a strong secret is configured while the deployment continues to use an attacker-derivable value. In OIDCSessionType client-cookie deployments, an unauthenticated remote attacker can derive the encryption key and forge a mod_auth_openidc_session cookie for another user, while server-cache deployments permit lower-impact tampering with protected OIDC state and nonce cookies. This issue is fixed in Open OnDemand versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3 and ood-ansible version 4.2.1.

title: Zyrabit Platform provides sovereign AI infrastructure for enterprise retrieval-augmented generation.
summary: Zyrabit Platform provides sovereign AI infrastructure for enterprise retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 2.4.4, import_to_vault(source_path, destination_name) accepts both caller-controlled paths, but the content-pattern guard does not confine destination_name. The vulnerable tool is implemented in zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/domain/services/mcp_service.py, where Path(DOCS_DIR) / destination_name is passed to shutil.copy2, allowing traversal or an absolute destination to write outside the vault. An unrestricted source_path can be copied into the vault and retrieved through secure_query, disclosing files readable by the service; files that do not match the executable-pattern filter pass that filter. When ENABLE_LEGACY_EXTENSIONS=true, zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/main.py registers POST /mcp/rpc without get_current_user, allowing unauthenticated network tool calls; this optional exposure is disabled by default and is not required for local invocation. If an attacker can stage chosen source content and write to an execution-triggered destination, the advisory describes conditional process execution. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.4.

title: The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames.
summary: The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.

title: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, a broker with a listener that is configured to use the PROXY protocol v2 is vulnerable to a...
summary:
In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, a broker with a listener that is configured to use the PROXY protocol v2 is vulnerable to an untrusted proxy providing details that cause the broker to accept fake SSL information.



This can be mitigated by following the documented requirements for PROXY listeners: It is very important that only trusted proxies are allowed to connect to any listener using the PROXY protocol, and that clients are not allowed to connect to the listener at all.

title: SmarterTools SmarterMail Insufficient Entropy Authentication Bypass Vulnerability.
summary:
SmarterTools SmarterMail Insufficient Entropy Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of SmarterTools SmarterMail. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the generation of Application Passwords. The issue results from using insufficient entropy in the generation of credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to bypass authentication on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-33568.

title: The NFC authentication handshake relies on a fixed, static challenge instead of a unique, random value for every session.
summary: The NFC authentication handshake relies on a fixed, static challenge instead of a unique, random value for every session. This allows an attacker to perform a "replay attack," successfully authenticating by simply sending the same pre-recorded response.

title: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository.
summary: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, a registered host or a party with its host/API credential can submit package metadata. Inventory reporting accepts package name and version, while available-update reporting accepts package name, version, and repository; the repository field exists only on that path. RepoManager stores these values, and stored values are rendered on the host's package detail page without preventing stored HTML or JavaScript from executing. An administrator must later view the page for script execution. The script runs in the administrator's authenticated browser session and can expose administrative data or forge privileged requests; the advisory describes possible escalation through admin-only functionality. Fixed in 5.13.3.

state-changing installation tasks without checking whether the shop is already

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
summary: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.3, src/Chamilo/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php and src/CourseBundle/Component/CourseCopy/CourseRestorer.php use paths supplied by an imported legacy course backup without consistently confining them to the extraction directory. A course teacher can import a crafted backup containing parent-directory path segments, causing file operations to write attacker-controlled content outside the intended destination, including PHP-executable or automatically loaded locations. This can result in code execution as the PHP process and compromise course data, user data, credentials, and the host. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.3.

title: Refitter allows arbitrary code execution through unescaped OpenAPI content-type values
summary: ### Summary Refitter emits the spec's content-type key (content map key in requestBody/responses) verbatim into a Refit `[Headers("Accept: <ct>", "Content-Type: <ct>")]` attribute string without escaping `"`. A crafted value survives Refitter's default OpenAPI validation, breaks out of the attribute and the enclosing interface + namespace, injects a top-level `file class` with a `[ModuleInitializer]` method, and reopens so the file stays valid. .NET runs `[ModuleInitializer]` methods at assembly load, so the attacker's code executes at application startup. Verified on Refitter 2.0.0 / .NET 8.
