title: The ownCloud Desktop Client synchronizes files between an ownCloud server and a desktop.
summary: The ownCloud Desktop Client synchronizes files between an ownCloud server and a desktop. Prior to 6.0.2, an authenticated attacker can share a specially crafted file with a victim. If the file is synced by the client and revealed in the macOS Finder, it can cause operating-system command injection on the victim’s computer. This issue is fixed in version 6.0.2.

title: This High severity Security Misconfiguration vulnerability was introduced in versions 10.2.0, 11.0.0, 12.0.0, and 12.1.0 of Bamboo Data C...
summary:
This High severity Security Misconfiguration vulnerability was introduced in versions 10.2.0, 11.0.0, 12.0.0, and 12.1.0 of Bamboo Data Center.

This Security Misconfiguration vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 8.9, allows an authenticated attacker to to get into the system utilizing loopholes exposed from security best-practices being overlooked.

Atlassian recommends that Bamboo Data Center customers upgrade to latest version, if you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to one of the specified supported fixed versions:
 Bamboo Data Center 10.2: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 10.2.26

 Bamboo Data Center 12.1: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 12.1.13

 Bamboo Data Center 13.0: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 13.0.1

See the release notes ([https://confluence.atlassian.com/bambooreleases/bamboo-release-notes-1189793869.html]). You can download the latest version of Bamboo Data Center from the download center ([https://www.atlassian.com/software/bamboo/download-archives]).

This vulnerability was reported via our Atlassian (Internal) program.

title: In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips o...
summary: In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 9.4.17, 10.0.12, 10.2.9, and 10.4.5, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles can...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 9.4.17, 10.0.12, 10.2.9, and 10.4.5, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles can configure a metric alert through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API that runs a search with elevated privileges. The vulnerability lets the user access or modify data and disrupt the Splunk Enterprise instance.
The vulnerability occurs because Splunk Enterprise does not enforce the required role-based authorization when it processes metric alert configuration through the REST API. Splunk Enterprise schedules the resulting search with elevated authorization and runs attacker-controlled search processing with that authorization.
For more information see About configuring role-based user access (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/about-configuring-role-based-user-access) in the Splunk documentation.

title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles cou...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could cause Splunk Enterprise to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with elevated privileges through data model acceleration.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly neutralize caller-supplied data model acceleration values before it places them into generated summarization searches.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to create and run playbooks could start child playbooks on con...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to create and run playbooks could start child playbooks on containers outside the authorized label, or repository scope for that user. This could expose container data and affect automation outside that scope.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not bind the identity used to authorize the child playbook run to the parent playbook execution context.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view and edit containers for one label could use a slash co...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view and edit containers for one label could use a slash command through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API to access sensitive product data and credentials outside the authorized container scope.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not enforce authorization for related objects that slash commands access from an authorized artifact.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with repository edit access could cause Splunk SOAR to write files outside the...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with repository edit access could cause Splunk SOAR to write files outside the configured repository, which lets the user modify files that the user account running Splunk SOAR can write to.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not require source control repository paths to remain inside the configured repository.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit permission could cause Splunk SOAR to execute arbitrary ...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit permission could cause Splunk SOAR to execute arbitrary code on the host when the user validates an installed app.
The vulnerability is possible because the app validation workflow does not isolate untrusted code from the trusted environment.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with only the apps:edit permission could install a connector app that cause...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with only the apps:edit permission could install a connector app that causes Splunk SOAR to write attacker-controlled files outside the app directory. This could let the user modify files used by Splunk SOAR and execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR constructs the dependency installation command from app-supplied metadata without preventing that metadata from changing its arguments.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Add and configure apps and assets to provide actions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.6.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-apps-and-assets/add-and-configure-apps-and-assets-to-provide-actions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit permission could execute arbitrary code as the user acco...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit permission could execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR by installing a malicious app.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not restrict app dependencies to validated binary packages before installing them.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Assets edit or delete permission and access to one or more tenants...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Assets edit or delete permission and access to one or more tenants could change or delete assets assigned to other tenants through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. With this access, the user could redirect connector traffic and expose the credentials and operational data associated with an asset, or disrupt integrations and data ingestion for other tenants.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR verifies the Assets edit or delete permission but does not verify that the user can access every tenant assigned to the target asset before Splunk SOAR changes or deletes the asset.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), Configure multiple tenants on your Splunk SOAR (On-premises) instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/configure-multiple-tenants-on-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance), Add and configure apps and assets to provide actions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.6.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-apps-and-assets/add-and-configure-apps-and-assets-to-provide-actions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), and Using the REST API reference for Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/8.5.0/using-the-splunk-soar-rest-api/using-the-rest-api-reference-for-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with edit permission for the container label on a pending approval could read ...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with edit permission for the container label on a pending approval could read an external-prompt capability through an Approval details Representational State Transfer (REST) API response and use it to view the prompt content, change the pending approval decision, and modify its action parameters.
The vulnerability is possible because an Approval details response exposes the external-prompt capability without checking approval ownership.
For more information see REST External Prompt (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/8.5.0/external-prompt-endpoints/rest-external-prompt) and Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.5.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

title: In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user who can influence indexed event data could store attacker-con...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user who can influence indexed event data could store attacker-controlled values in event fields. If another authenticated user who reviews the event selects the View Adaptive Response Invocations or View Adaptive Response Results workflow action from Event Actions, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the action. The unauthenticated user could then access or modify sensitive data and disrupt services available to the user who selects the action.
The vulnerability is possible because the affected Common Information Model workflow actions insert the orig_sid and orig_rid event-field values directly into searches without safely validating or quoting the values.
For more information see About workflow actions in Splunk Web (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.2/workflow-actions/about-workflow-actions-in-splunk-web) in the Splunk documentation.

title: In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_investigation_read capability could cause the Ri...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_investigation_read capability could cause the Risk Event Timeline Representational State Transfer (REST) API to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could expose stored credentials and modify indexes and lookup data available to those permissions.
The vulnerability is possible because the affected REST API does not validate request values before including them in search macro arguments.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Risk analysis (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/risk-analysis) in the Splunk documentation.

title: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository.
summary: RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, an authenticated user can supply a user-controlled, array-valued GPG key identifier to the key deletion action. Validate::string() filters HTML characters but not shell metacharacters. The user-controlled identifier reaches the delete action without shell-safe encoding. controllers/Gpg.php contains the vulnerable deletion path. Process::execute() passes the command string through proc_open() and /bin/sh -c, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands as the web/PHP process. This can expose secrets or poison packages. Authentication is required, but the advisory makes an administrator-only restriction conditional on the intended access policy and does not establish an administrator role as a prerequisite. Fixed in 5.13.3.

title: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allows malicious serve...
summary: ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Decode in src/Bitmap.c that allows malicious servers to corrupt client memory by sending a PNG with a duplicate IHDR chunk. Attackers can supply crafted PNGs via texture pack URLs or player skins so the unreset bufferIdx underflows remaining space, letting IDAT data overflow the buffer to crash clients or execute code.

title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the BCF reader can experience an integer overflow in a record-length check that verifies whether a record contains enough bytes for the expected number and size of stored items. A crafted BCF record can bypass this check, causing reads beyond the stored data and, in some cases, writes beyond the heap buffer when the reader sets the least significant bit of accessed bytes. Opening such a file can crash the process, corrupt data or heap structures, and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the CRAM decoder validates the 254-character query-name limit only after decoding the name into a 1024-byte stack array. An attacker-controlled CRAM record can provide an overlong query name and overflow the local stack buffer before the later validation runs; all CRAM format versions are affected. Opening such a file can crash the process, corrupt stack data, and may permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, the experimental CRAM v4 XPACK and XRLE decoders cache expanded block pointers at indexes beyond the 512-element slice->block_by_id array. An array index partially controlled by data in the input file first causes an out-of-bounds read to determine whether a block is cached; a null value then causes allocation of a block and an out-of-bounds pointer write to the same element. The invalid read may crash the process, while the write may corrupt heap state and could permit arbitrary code execution. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

title: PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.
summary:
PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title: obsidian-sync-mcp: Missing Host/Origin validation lets a public website drive a victim's Obsidian vault via DNS rebinding (no-auth mode)
summary: When obsidian-sync-mcp runs without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN (the documented no-auth mode for local use), the HTTP MCP endpoint does not validate the Host or Origin header before dispatching MCP methods (CWE-350). title: NotrinosERP is an open-source web-based enterprise resource planning system written in PHP and MySQL.
summary: NotrinosERP is an open-source web-based enterprise resource planning system written in PHP and MySQL. From 1.0.0 until 1.1.0, the employee document handler in hrm/manage/employees.php allows an authenticated user with SA_EMPLOYEE permission to submit doc_file through tab_documents() and stores the raw client filename, including an executable extension, under company/0/documents/employees/ without extension, MIME, or content validation. Uploading a PHP file places executable content beneath the web root, where requesting the stored file results in server-side code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0.

title: mssql-mcp-core: SQL injection in mssql-mcp write tools via unparameterized table names and WHERE clauses
summary: Several tools in `mssql-mcp-core` built T-SQL by string-interpolating caller-supplied identifiers and predicates directly into the statement passed to the node-mssql `Request.query()` batch API. Only data values were parameterized. Affected tools and inputs: - `update_data`, `delete_data`: `tableName` and the free-form `whereClause` were interpolated raw. - `insert_data`: `tableName` and column names (object keys) were interpolated raw. - `execute_transaction`: the same raw `tableName`/`whereClause` interpolation per operation. - `create_table`, `create_index`, `drop_table`: table/column/index

title: An authenticated iControl SOAP user with at least Guest access can inject an unauthorized management request.
summary:
An authenticated iControl SOAP user with at least Guest access can inject an unauthorized management request.





Impact:

This vulnerability may allow an authenticated attacker with network access and at least Guest role privileges to the iControl SOAP utility to execute arbitrary system commands, create or delete files, or disable services. There is no data plane exposure; this is a control plane issue only.





Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

summary:
Latvijas Valsts radio un televīzijas centrs (LVRTC)
eParakstītājs 3.0 version 1.10.0-resolute allows an unauthenticated remote
attacker to cause HTTP GET requests from a user's workstation by convincing the
user to open a crafted signed eDOC file. Automatic certificate validation
retrieves a signer-controlled Authority Information Access (AIA) caIssuers URL
and follows redirects without restricting the destination, enabling blind SSRF
to loopback and private-network services. Additionally, unrestricted loading of
local file URIs (such as file:///dev/zero) causes unbounded memory buffering
resulting in Denial of Service (OutOfMemoryError). In automated server
verification pipelines with UI:N, impact scales up to CVSS 8.6 High.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack p...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer

The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated
buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync).
However, this pointer is not cleared when the function returns.

If an event is processed (e.g. by a different thread) while the
send_mutex is held by a new command, but before that command has
updated send_receive_buf, the handler (hidpp_raw_hidpp_event) will
observe that the mutex is locked and dereference the stale pointer.

This results in an out-of-bounds access on a different thread's kernel
stack (or a NULL pointer dereference on the very first command).

Fix this by:
1. Clearing hidpp->send_receive_buf to NULL before releasing the mutex
   in the synchronous command path.
2. Moving the assignment of the local 'question' and 'answer' pointers
   inside the mutex_is_locked() block in the handler, and adding
   a NULL check before dereferencing.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

For...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.  Even though
it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active,
there's zero value in not handling SMM.  At that point, the only scenario
where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the
vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those
modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the
MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides
most of the re-configuration in that case).

Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an
unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while
L2 is active.

Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even
though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT
events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when
CR0.PG must be '0').

title: Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Accessory Protocol chacha20_decrypt Integer Underflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability.
summary:
Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Accessory Protocol chacha20_decrypt Integer Underflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Philips Hue Bridge. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the HomeKit Accessory Protocol service, which listens on TCP port 8080 by default. When parsing pairing requests, the process does not properly validate user-supplied data, which can result in an integer underflow before writing to memory. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28332.

title: Philips Hue Bridge hap_pair_setup_handler Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability.
summary:
Philips Hue Bridge hap_pair_setup_handler Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Philips Hue Bridge. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the HomeKit Accessory Protocol service, which listens on TCP port 8080 by default. When parsing pairing requests, the process does not properly validate the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length, heap-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28434.

title: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions.
summary: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.9.1, web/controle/control.php authorizes FuncionarioControle requests only by checking whether an authenticated employee has a permission row for resource 11 or 91, while MiddlewareDAO::verificarPermissao() does not compare the stored id_acao value or authorize the requested method. An employee with any such permission and a valid CSRF token from the employee's own session can invoke FuncionarioControle::adicionarPermissao, FuncionarioControle::alterarPermissao, or FuncionarioControle::excluirPermissao to add, change, or remove permissions for arbitrary roles. This can grant higher action levels over sensitive resources, expose or modify protected employee, patient, configuration, and administrative data, or disrupt legitimate access by changing other roles. This issue is fixed in version 3.9.1.

title: Servo is a lightweight, high-performance web rendering engine for embedding web technologies in applications.
summary: Servo is a lightweight, high-performance web rendering engine for embedding web technologies in applications. Prior to 0.4.0, a frame with sandbox="" can reach and execute a javascript: URL through declarative refresh because RefreshRedirectDue::invoke() in components/script/dom/document/document.rs can reach JavaScript URL handling in components/script/script_thread.rs without enforcing the sandbox's script prohibition. This gives attacker-controlled content arbitrary JavaScript execution in a frame intended to be scriptless, including nested DOM probe creation and blind browser requests. The frame retains an opaque origin, so the issue does not by itself provide parent DOM access. This issue is fixed in version 0.4.0.

title: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker.
summary: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, check_client_auth() in src/api/auth.c detects that a matching session identifier has passed valid_until but still assigns user_id before the expired state can be rejected. That assignment sends execution through the authorized branch, renews valid_until for another timeout interval, and leaves the session-expired response unreachable. An attacker who possesses a previously valid session identifier can periodically reuse it to preserve administrative access indefinitely, making the configured session timeout ineffective. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

title: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business.
summary: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264, the routes for PluginService::regenerateSecret and PluginService::delete carry no @Permissions decorator, and the methods omit plugin ownership checks. An authenticated attacker can directly target another plugin's identifier to rotate and disclose its OAuth secret or delete the plugin, including system plugins. Separately, PermissionGuard authorizes several nested API requests using a caller-controlled parent tableId, baseId, or spaceId, while the services resolve the requested child object only by its globally unique identifier. An authenticated attacker can provide a parent resource the attacker owns together with a victim's child identifier. ViewService::getViewById can then disclose another tenant's view configuration, embedded filter values, field layout, and shareId. DashboardService::updatePluginStorage and the view-position updatePluginStorage path can overwrite another tenant's plugin storage because the plugin installation is not rebound to the authorized base, dashboard, table, or view. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264.

title: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business.
summary: Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.

title:

ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc()

...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check in build_sec_desc()

When the large dacl_offset is provided, dacl_offset + sizeof(struct
smb_acl) overflows on 32-bit builds and the check is passed,
Which makes le16_to_cpu(ppdacl_ptr->size) read out-of-bounds. This
only happens for dacl_offset in range [0xFFFFFFF8, 0xFFFFFFFF]. So
the oob read is max 8 bytes preceding the allocated ppntsd.

    unsigned int dacl_offset = le32_to_cpu(ppntsd->dacloffset);
    int ppdacl_size, ntacl_size = ppntsd_size - dacl_offset;

    if (!dacl_offset ||
	(dacl_offset + sizeof(struct smb_acl) > ppntsd_size))
	    goto out;

Commit beff0bc9d69b ("ksmbd: fix overflow in dacloffset bounds check")
fixes similar checks in other functions. But leaves this one out,
because it is only valid for 32-bit builds.

Reproduced on 32-bit ARM with KASAN, by a client sending SMB2
SET_INFO(SEC) with dacloffset=0xfffffff8, then QUERY_INFO(SEC) on the
same file:

 BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105)
 Read of size 2 at addr c2a273fa by task kworker/1:1/35
 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 35 Comm: kworker/1:1 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc2+ #5
 Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
 Call trace:
  kasan_check_range from build_sec_desc (fs/smb/server/smbacl.c:1105)
  build_sec_desc from smb2_query_info (fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c:7676)
  smb2_query_info from handle_ksmbd_work (fs/smb/server/server.c:160)
  handle_ksmbd_work from process_one_work (kernel/workqueue.c:3401)
  process_one_work from worker_thread (kernel/workqueue.c:3473)
  worker_thread from kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)

Add overflow check.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()

...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix slab-out-of-bounds write in id_mode_to_cifs_acl()

In id_mode_to_cifs_acl(), while the chown branch reserves
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_acl) and the worst-case ACE space after
commit 0ee150794c75 ("smb: client: fix heap overflow in DACL owner/group
rewrite")), the chmod branch only adds 2 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) or
5 * sizeof(struct smb_ace) to secdesclen (or 1 * sizeof(struct smb_ace)
on posix).

However, the chmod branch also invokes build_sec_desc() ->
copy_sec_desc(), which unconditionally writes the Owner SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset and the Group SID at
pnntsd + sidsoffset + sizeof(struct smb_sid) (2 * 68 = 136 bytes total),
and set_chmod_dacl() always writes a struct smb_acl header (8 bytes)
even when the source descriptor has dacloffset == 0. When a security
descriptor has compact or overlapping Owner/Group SIDs (or
dacloffset == 0), calling chmod() under-allocates pnntsd and writes past
the end of the slab buffer.

Reserve sizeof(struct smb_acl) + 2 * sizeof(struct smb_sid) (plus
sizeof(struct smb_ntsd) on the posix path) in the chmod branch of
id_mode_to_cifs_acl().

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix SMB2 CREATE response buffer overflow

smb2_allocate_rsp_b...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix SMB2 CREATE response buffer overflow

smb2_allocate_rsp_buf() uses the MAX_CIFS_SMALL_BUFFER_SIZE
(448-byte) buffer for a single SMB2_CREATE response. That buffer also
holds a 4-byte length field, which only leaves 444 bytes for the SMB2
body.

The AAPL response made this buffer too small. After 8f1b796ff113, a
request with AAPL response contexts may need at least 456 bytes. In
the 456-byte case, create_aapl_rsp_buf() is appended last, clears 128
bytes, and writes 12 bytes past the allocation.

KASAN reports:

    BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0
    Write of size 128 at addr ffff88800370954c by task kworker/0:0/9
    ...
    create_aapl_rsp_buf+0x31/0x6e0
    smb2_open+0x58f9/0xef10
    ...
    smb2_allocate_rsp_buf+0x19d/0x370
    ...
    The buggy address is located 332 bytes inside of
     allocated 448-byte region [ffff888003709400, ffff8880037095c0)

Reserve enough space for any fixed CREATE response KSMBD can build.
Store the required allocation size in the per-dialect values table.
This keeps the small buffer for other commands and avoids using the max
transaction buffer for every CREATE.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix app-instance non-durable supersede session UAF

ksmbd_clo...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix app-instance non-durable supersede session UAF

ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id() supersedes a prior open that has the
same AppInstanceId. It reaches that open's session through opinfo->sess.
This pointer is not refcounted.

Session teardown detaches durable handles before it frees the session.
It does not detach a non-durable open. That open still points at the
session through opinfo->sess after the session is freed. Another session
can supersede the open at the same time. The supersede then takes a
write lock through the stale pointer, in the freed session's file table.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0
  Call Trace:
   _raw_write_lock+0x71/0xd0
   ksmbd_close_fd_app_instance_id+0xd9/0x670 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x3e10/0xd910 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 212:
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0x38d/0x480 [ksmbd]

Fix this by looking the session up by opinfo->session_id. The lookup
returns a reference, as smb2_break_collect_channels() does. Recheck that
opinfo->sess still points at it before using it.

Do the lookup without m_lock held. destroy_previous_session() takes
m_lock under the session table lock, and taking them in the other order
here would deadlock.

Because the compact index served to clients is line-based, a user who can publish a gem to an owner's registry could forge index entries, such as packages that do not exist or additional versions of an existing gem with dependencies of their choice. Clients that resolve gems from that registry could then be led to install attacker-chosen dependencies. Gems with such metadata are now rejected.

title: A repository created with auto-init accepted pushes before its initialization had finished, and the initial commit was built in a checkou...
summary: A repository created with auto-init accepted pushes before its initialization had finished, and the initial commit was built in a checkout of whatever the repository already contained. A user who is allowed to create repositories could push a crafted tree during that window so that writing the README followed a symbolic link and overwrote a server-side git hook, which runs commands as the Gitea system user. The initial commit is now built in a freshly initialized directory, and a new repository only becomes ready, and accepts pushes, once its initialization is complete.

title: Open Access Management (OpenAM) is an access management solution.
summary: Open Access Management (OpenAM) is an access management solution. Prior to 16.1.1, the `Cross-Domain Single Sign-On` (`CDSSO`) servlet allows a logged-in user's raw OpenAM session token to be POSTed to an attacker-controlled URL. An attacker who induces an authenticated victim to visit a crafted URL can receive the session credential and potentially hijack the session. Deployments must have `CDSSO` enabled, as is common in multi-domain deployments, and exploitation is additionally gated on a non-default configuration being absent. This issue is fixed in version 16.1.1.

title: The LeRobot library is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution via unsafe dynamic class instantiation in the from_pretrained() method and ...
summary: The LeRobot library is vulnerable to arbitrary code execution via unsafe dynamic class instantiation in the from_pretrained() method and related paths. When loading a policy's processor configuration from a repository,  the library uses the class field within the JSON configuration to dynamically resolve and instantiate Python classes using importlib.import_module() and getattr().

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.7.0, a user that has the "Observer" role could use query filters in the Representational State Transfer (...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.7.0, a user that has the "Observer" role could use query filters in the Representational State Transfer (REST) API to infer password hashes and authorization tokens for other users.
The information disclosure is possible because Splunk SOAR applies REST API query filters to user records before it protects sensitive fields from query processing.
For more information see Using the REST API reference for Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/8.5.0/using-the-splunk-soar-rest-api/using-the-rest-api-reference-for-splunk-soar-on-premises), Query for Data (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/7.1.0/using-the-splunk-soar-rest-api/query-for-data), and Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.5.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

summary: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser does not enforce limits on encoded variable-length fields controlled by a remote peer. A remote peer can cause the decoder to buffer data indefinitely until memory is exhausted, causing denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

title: In the Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library, outbound HTTP requests are not restricted to the configured Okta organization domain when proc...
summary: In the Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library, outbound HTTP requests are not restricted to the configured Okta organization domain when processing certain URL formats. If a URL parameter is modified to specify an external host, the library may transmit the configured SSWS API token to that unintended destination.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with the containers:edit permission could import a container that includes a malicious Hypert...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with the containers:edit permission could import a container that includes a malicious Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) note. When another user views the imported note, Splunk SOAR could run unauthorized JavaScript in the browser of that user, exposing data and allowing actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not sanitize HTML note content during container import before it renders the content in Mission Control.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for a container or workbook task could store attacker-controlled Hyperte...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for a container or workbook task could store attacker-controlled Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) in a note. When another user with view permission for the affected container and its notes opens the affected note in Mission Control, the note could run unauthorized JavaScript code in the browser of that user, expose data available through the authenticated session, and perform actions available through the authenticated session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not neutralize active content in all notes before Mission Control renders them.

title: aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client.
summary: aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client. From 0.11.0 until 0.11.4, add_subscription() in amqtt/broker.py accepts malformed single-level + wildcard placement because it checks substrings instead of validating each slash-delimited level. The _matches() function converts each + into a greedy regular-expression fragment and evaluates it with re.fullmatch(), allowing a filter containing many adjacent + characters to trigger catastrophic backtracking when compared with a topic that partially matches but ultimately fails. Because matching runs synchronously in _run_broadcast(), one subscription followed by a publish can block the broker event loop, stopping message delivery and new connection processing until restart. Anonymous clients can trigger the issue with the default configuration. Any authenticated client permitted to create arbitrary subscriptions and publish messages may still exploit it when authentication is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.4.

summary: Joomla Extension - akeeba.com - Account takeover through missing OAuth state validation in Akeeba SocialLogin extension 1.0.0-4.11.0 - The OAuth callback did not validate a session-bound state parameter, allowing an attacker to link their own social provider identity to the account of a logged-in user who opens a crafted callback link and subsequently log in as that user.

title: Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.
summary:
Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.

The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

title:
The administration page "Offene
Bestellungen" (open orders) of the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin for JTL-Shop outputs the
customer name of p...
summary:
The administration page "Offene
Bestellungen" (open orders) of the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin for JTL-Shop outputs the
customer name of pending orders without output encoding. A registered
customer (free self-registration) can submit an HTML-entity-encoded name, which is
decoded to markup when the billing address of an order is written. If
the PayPal payment is left unfinished, the order is listed on the page and the
name is rendered as markup in the browser of an administrator who opens
the page. The script code runs with the privileges of that administrator
and can, for example, create a new administrator account. Guest orders are
not affected, because the name is encoded again.

title: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS).
summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, a user-controlled schedule appName is joined into the schedule directory path and interpolated without shell quoting into commands that create the directory and write the schedule script. An authenticated user who can create or update a dokploy-server schedule can inject operating-system commands that execute with the Dokploy process privileges when the schedule is saved, including root privileges on typical installations. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.

title: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics.
summary: MyMangaDB is a self-hosted manga collection manager with automatic metadata, MyAnimeList import, Docker support, and collection statistics. Prior to 2.7.2, the unauthenticated /api/v1/database/export handler in backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/database.py returns a ZIP containing the live SQLite database and the cover-image library. The database includes the users table and hashed_password values, allowing a remote attacker to obtain all application data and conduct offline password attacks without a session or token. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.2.

title: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms.
summary: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms stores attacker-influenceable job output that server/src/lib/common.js processes through formatOutput without HTML escaping and client/src/components/AppAnsibleOutput.vue renders through v-html. An authenticated user can submit job input that is echoed into persistent output, causing script execution when another user views the job. Additional designer-controlled HTML and expression values reach v-html in client/src/components/AppForm.vue and client/src/components/BsInputForForm.vue without sanitization. Because Content Security Policy is disabled and the JWT is stored in localStorage, script execution can steal a victim's token and take over the account, including an administrator account. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.1.

title: A caller who can reach the temporal-proxy gRPC listener, with or without a valid credential, can grow the proxy's memory until the proces...
summary: A caller who can reach the temporal-proxy gRPC listener, with or without a valid credential, can grow the proxy's memory until the process is terminated by sending requests with many distinct gRPC method names. temporal-proxy labels its request metrics with the method name exactly as the caller sent it, and records every request, including those that authentication or routing reject. Each distinct method name adds metric series that are never removed. The series grow whether or not the metrics endpoint is scraped, and metric labels configured from request metadata multiply the growth. temporal-proxy versions 0.1.0-alpha.20260716 through 1.2.0 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line.

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
summary: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40, main/dropbox/dropbox_functions.inc.php accepts a literal .htaccess filename in the course dropbox and stores it in a directory served by Apache, where the file can alter handler behavior under the required AllowOverride All configuration. Any authenticated course participant can upload .htaccess and then upload a PHP payload disguised as a .gif, resulting in code execution as the web-server user when the dropbox tool is enabled. This can expose or modify the Chamilo installation, course content, and database credentials. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40.

title: LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via unrestricted upload of dangerous file types in the service ticket ...
summary:
LMS (Lan Management System) is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via unrestricted upload of dangerous file types in the service ticket feature of the client panel. The application does not verify the type or name of files attached to service tickets. An authenticated attacker can upload an .htaccess file to bypass the access restrictions on the storage directory, together with a PHP script. Visiting the uploaded PHP file's URL leads to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the web server.


This issue was fixed in commit 89dd3f7.

title: CAST Imaging contains a hardcoded authentication token in the "KeyCloakController" class of auth-service.jar.
summary:
CAST Imaging contains a hardcoded authentication token in the "KeyCloakController" class of auth-service.jar. An attacker who gains access to the source code, application package, logs, or configuration files can reuse this token to call auth-service endpoints without authentication. Using the token with the "/api/auth/keycloak/users" endpoint, the attacker can enumerate users across Keycloak realms and retrieve user attributes containing API token hashes, enabling reconnaissance and further exploitation.


The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

title: Dell PowerStore contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.
summary: Dell PowerStore contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. An authenticated user with limited privileges could potentially exploit this vulnerability to make the appliance connect to attacker-chosen internal systems.

title: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth token holders to act as full sessions because O...
summary: NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth token holders to act as full sessions because OAuth access tokens are signed with the instance JWT secret. Attackers can present a narrowly scoped OAuth token to the session strategy, short-lived-token exchange, or NocoSocket handshake to gain the granting user's full privileges.

title: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute...
summary: NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute script by injecting markup into fields rendered through URL() formulas. The canvas grid renderer assigns unsanitized formula output to innerHTML, letting attackers steal session tokens from localStorage and take over accounts of users viewing the table.

title: WWBN AVideo from 6.5 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with upload permission to inject script by su...
summary: WWBN AVideo from 6.5 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with upload permission to inject script by submitting a javascript: scheme videoLink for embed videos. The unvalidated URL is rendered into an iframe src in videoEmbeded.php and PlayerSkins.php, executing for viewers including administrators and enabling creation of new administrator accounts.

title: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command in certain ASUS Router firmware models allows an remote attacker to to ...
summary:
Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command in certain ASUS Router firmware models allows an remote attacker to to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges by inducing a logged-in administrator to visit a malicious website.
Refer to the ' Security Update for ASUS Router Firmware ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

title: Vulnerability in the Oracle Access Manager product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Authentication Engine).
summary: Vulnerability in the Oracle Access Manager product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Authentication Engine).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.1.0. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via SAML to compromise Oracle Access Manager.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle Access Manager, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Access Manager accessible data as well as  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Access Manager accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.7 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N).

title: Instatic is an open source visual content management system for building static websites.
summary: Instatic is an open source visual content management system for building static websites. Prior to 0.0.14, isSafeUrl() and safeUrl() in src/core/html-sanitize/index.ts remove tabs, newlines, carriage returns, and characters handled by String.prototype.trim(), but leave other leading C0 control characters that browsers discard before parsing a URL scheme. A low-privileged editor can place a dangerous URL behind one of those controls in a URL property or custom HTML attribute, allowing src/core/publisher/escapeProps.ts and the shared URL sanitizer to emit it into rendered content. When an Owner or Admin activates the element in the same-origin admin editor canvas, script executes with the victim's application authority and can drive admin APIs to read protected data, create an owner account, or install a plugin. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.14.

title: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database.
summary: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.30.0 until 0.40.3, an authenticated Agent with folder write access can use POST /upload to store HTML or SVG content that GET /download/{path} serves from the application origin through server/src/handlers/download.rs. The response sets Content-Disposition: inline and lacks forced attachment handling and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, allowing the browser to render the uploaded active content as the application. When a victim opens the link, the script can access the JavaScript-readable atomic_session cookie and the Agent private key in same-origin IndexedDB, enabling persistent account impersonation. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

title: Effect: ReDoS in Schema.TemplateLiteral compiled regex
summary: ### Impact `Schema.TemplateLiteral` compiles each `Schema.String` span to the lazy wildcard `[\s\S]*?` and decodes input by running the resulting regular expression against it. When a template has two or more `Schema.String` spans, for example: ```ts Schema.TemplateLiteral(Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, "X") ``` the regex contains several ambiguous wildcards. A non-matching input makes the backtracking engine try combinations across all of them, so matching time grows cubically with input length. title: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implem...
summary: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, after FreeSWITCH has learned and closed source learning for an RTP peer, read_rtp_packet() and rtp_common_read() in src/switch_rtp.c reject RTP from an unrecognized source only after packet classification and, for encrypted calls, SRTP processing. An unauthenticated attacker with UDP reachability to an active RTP or SRTP media port can sustain a foreign-source packet flood that occupies the media read path and prevents legitimate media from entering FreeSWITCH on calls that consume incoming media for relay or echo. The resulting one-way audio allows the affected endpoint to continue hearing the other party, but the other party loses that endpoint's audio, leaving SIP signaling established while the call is unusable for conversation. Transmit-only playback was unaffected in testing. A caller can learn the media port from the SDP answer, while a third party must first discover an active port, and no valid SRTP key is required. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

title: Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js.
summary: Wiki.js is an open source wiki app built on Node.js. Prior to 2.5.315, an authenticated user with write:pages can store JavaScript expressions in the v-slot:tabs or v-slot:content attributes of page HTML because server/modules/rendering/html-security/renderer.js adds those executable Vue directives to DOMPurify's allowlist. The sanitized output is inserted as rendered page HTML and later compiled by the Vue 2 runtime compiler, so the expressions execute in the Wiki.js origin when another user views the page even when the author lacks write:scripts and administrative permissions. The script runs with the viewer's browser session and can read same-origin data, modify displayed content, present phishing content, or perform actions available to that viewer, including privileged GraphQL operations when a privileged user opens the page. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.315.

title: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files.
summary: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 1.3.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not correctly filter the limited set of options permitted in a repository's .lfsconfig file when option keys contain certain additional components. Crafted keys can mimic options that configure Git LFS to use a custom command to transfer objects, causing Git LFS to execute an attacker-selected command or binary while fetching objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

title: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files.
summary: Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 0.6.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS reads Git configuration options defined for a submodule without checking certain values for embedded line-ending control characters. A malicious repository can insert control characters such as line feed (LF) into those values to mimic options that cause Git LFS to execute an attacker-controlled command or binary while fetching or adding objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

title: Cross-site scripting in the embedded co-browsing feature in Unblu inc.
summary:
Cross-site scripting in the embedded co-browsing feature in Unblu inc. Unblu Spark 7.0 through 7.57.9 and 8.0 before 8.40.2, on on-premises and cloud deployments, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker in the visitor role to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of an agent taking part in the attacker's co-browsing session, via manipulated synchronized page attributes of the co-browsed page.



The JavaScript runs in the context and under the identity of the agent's session in the Agent Desk or the Single Conversation Desk.



Exploitation requires an agent to join an embedded co-browsing session with the attacker. Mobile co-apping isn't affected.

title: An SSH certificate authentication bypass vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed an authenticated organization member to read a...
summary: An SSH certificate authentication bypass vulnerability in GitHub Enterprise Server allowed an authenticated organization member to read and modify another user's private repositories within the trusted certificate authority's scope. Exploitation required an instance using built-in authentication and a valid certificate issued to the attacker by a trusted SSH certificate authority. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

title: The Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library systematically writes per-request authentication credentials to a shared HTTP client instance, rat...
summary: The Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library systematically writes per-request authentication credentials to a shared HTTP client instance, rather than being isolated to individual outbound request objects. When using scoped child clients, a subsequent scoped request can overwrite the shared client configuration. Because the original parent client credential has not been restored, subsequent outbound requests may be transmitted using the newly written credential, which can result in subsequent actions being executed under the context of an incorrect security principal in the Okta Management API and improper attribution in audit logs.

summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). title: Linux Mint Update Manager manages software updates on Linux Mint systems.
summary: Linux Mint Update Manager manages software updates on Linux Mint systems. From 5.4.8 until 5.5.4.3, 5.5.9.1, 5.8.8.1, 5.9.8.1, 6.0.9.1, and 6.1.5.1, mint-refresh-cache passes a user-controlled --parent-window-id value directly to the privileged Synaptic process without validating it as an integer. A local user permitted to execute mint-refresh-cache through sudo can inject additional Synaptic command-line options and achieve arbitrary code execution as root. title: In nanobot, when sandboxed exec is enabled, the shell executable used to run commands can be selected by the caller and is launched befor...
summary:
In nanobot, when sandboxed exec is enabled, the shell executable used to run commands can be selected by the caller and is launched before the sandbox is applied. An attacker who can induce the agent to create an executable in the workspace and select it as the shell can cause that executable to run outside the sandbox (e.g. Linux bubblewrap), with the operating-system permissions of the nanobot process.

This issue affects nanobot (nanobot-ai) from 0.2.1 before 0.4.1.

title: qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform.
summary: qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform. Prior to 2026.27, the privileged createFile helper followed attacker-controlled symbolic links during file creation. A local unprivileged user whose account is managed by the SSH Keys bundle could replace ~/.ssh with a link to /root/.ssh, causing the agent to write an authorized key for root. On systems using RAUC download mode with ineffective kernel symlink protection, the predictable /tmp/.bundle.raucb.part path could be linked to a system file and then overwritten or truncated during an update. A file-distribution destination beneath an attacker-controlled directory could similarly redirect the partial-download path so the agent changed ownership of a sensitive file. These vectors could result in root privilege escalation, arbitrary file modification, or denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 2026.27.

title: LibreOffice Base documents can bind macros to document events, such as opening or closing the document.
summary: LibreOffice Base documents can bind macros to document events, such as opening or closing the document. The macro security setting decides whether macros that come with a document may run. Macros bound to the events of a Base document were run without the macro security setting being applied, so opening or converting a crafted database document could run a macro and, through it, any command. In fixed versions macros bound to the events of a Base document follow the macro security setting, as macros in other documents do.

title: LibreOffice Calc can link a cell range to an external data source, and the link is saved in the document.
summary: LibreOffice Calc can link a cell range to an external data source, and the link is saved in the document. A Java database driver for such a link is loaded from a class path. Opening a crafted document could still load a Java database driver from a location outside the local machine and run its code, by a route that the fix for CVE-2026-63277 did not cover. In fixed versions an entry in a Java class path has to be a file URL that names a file on the local machine.

title: LibreOffice bundles the HSQLDB database engine, which can be used through the generic JDBC database driver as well as through the support...
summary: LibreOffice bundles the HSQLDB database engine, which can be used through the generic JDBC database driver as well as through the support for embedded databases. HSQLDB lets SQL statements call Java methods, limited to the classes that are permitted. When HSQLDB was used through the generic JDBC driver this limit did not apply, so SQL in a crafted document could call any Java method and run code. In fixed versions SQL can call only the built-in functions of HSQLDB, whichever way the database is reached.

title: LibreOffice can connect to databases through JDBC drivers written in Java.
summary: LibreOffice can connect to databases through JDBC drivers written in Java. A spreadsheet can use a database as the source of a pivot table, and the database document that describes the connection names the driver to use. The location the driver was loaded from was taken from the database document itself, so a crafted document could make LibreOffice load and run Java code that the document supplied when it was opened. This is a different route to the problem fixed for CVE-2026-63277. In fixed versions the driver location is taken only from the driver configuration of the user, and a pivot table whose source is a database document named by a URL connects only once the user allows links to be updated.

title: LibreOffice Writer can open HTML documents, and an HTML document can bind macros to events of the document as a whole, such as the docume...
summary: LibreOffice Writer can open HTML documents, and an HTML document can bind macros to events of the document as a whole, such as the document being opened or closed. Macros bound to these events were not taken into account by the macro security check, so they could run when the document was opened, whatever the macro security level. In fixed versions these macros follow the macro security settings like any other macro in the document.

title: LibreOffice documents in ODF format can contain form controls, such as buttons and text fields, and each control names the component that...
summary: LibreOffice documents in ODF format can contain form controls, such as buttons and text fields, and each control names the component that implements it. The component a control named was created even when it was not a form control, and the settings stored with the control were applied to it, so a crafted document could change the configuration of LibreOffice in a way that led to code being run. In fixed versions a control whose component is not a form control is ignored.

title: A document can carry its own user interface customizations, such as keyboard shortcuts, menus and toolbars, which take effect while the d...
summary: A document can carry its own user interface customizations, such as keyboard shortcuts, menus and toolbars, which take effect while the document is open. A command bound in these customizations could run a macro or a script even when the macro security settings did not allow the macros of the document, so a user who pressed a shortcut or chose a menu item in a crafted document could run code without any warning. In fixed versions the customizations of a document are treated like its other macro content, and the macro and script commands in them are only kept when the macros of the document are allowed.

title: An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and En...
summary: An uncontrolled search path vulnerability (CWE-427) in statically linked OpenSSL libraries within Netskope Client (stAgentSvc.exe) and Endpoint DLP (epdlp.exe) on Windows allows an authenticated local attacker to execute arbitrary code with elevated SYSTEM privileges. The services retain internal build-time paths referencing a secondary drive location. On Windows systems where default volume permissions allow standard users to create root-level directories on secondary drives, an attacker can place a malicious configuration file (openssl.cnf) that is loaded under the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM context upon service startup or system reboot. Under default operating system permissions, macOS and Linux are not susceptible, and mobile platforms are unaffected.

title: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer.
summary: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

title: A wide range of Harbor versions allow SSRF via its webhook delivery component which does not properly validate web hook target addresses,...
summary: A wide range of Harbor versions allow SSRF via its webhook delivery component which does not properly validate web hook target addresses, allowing usage of private and link-local IP ranges. An authenticated attacker with ProjectAdmin permissions can configure a webhook policy pointing to a private internal address. When a project event fires, Harbor jobservice makes unauthenticated outbound HTTP POST requests to the target. If the target answers with an error status, the response body is written to the webhook execution log, which project members can read, potentially exposing cloud metadata or other network-restricted resources.

summary:

We are not currently aware of malicious exploitation against ServiceNow instances. We recommend customers promptly apply appropriate updates or upgrade to a patched release if they have not already done so.

title: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal.
summary: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, the Open OnDemand dashboard includes noVNC passwords in query parameters generated by apps/dashboard/app/helpers/batch_connect/sessions_helper.rb and apps/dashboard/app/views/batch_connect/sessions/connections/_novnc.html.erb. The server records those query strings in per-user PUN access logs, and insufficiently protected log directories can allow another local user to recover and replay a launch URL. Replaying the credential grants access to the running remote desktop and can result in horizontal or vertical privilege escalation according to the privileges of the desktop owner. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3.

title: Tapir: Construction/decode RCE via property name -> raw case-class field (tapir-openapi-codegen)
summary: The OpenAPI code generator (tapir-openapi-codegen-core) builds Scala source by string templating and emitted several names/values from the (untrusted) OpenAPI document without escaping or validation, allowing injection of arbitrary Scala that runs at generated-code compile time and/or endpoint-assembly time (build/codegen-time RCE from an attacker-controlled spec).
