title: tcp_pkt_linearize() in subsys/net/ip/tcp.c is used by th_get() whenever a received TCP header is not contiguous in a single net_buf.
summary:
tcp_pkt_linearize() in subsys/net/ip/tcp.c is used by th_get() whenever a received TCP header is not contiguous in a single net_buf. While pulling the header bytes out of the following fragments, the loop called net_buf_unref() on an emptied fragment without first detaching its frags pointer. net_buf_unref() walks the whole fragment list, so the payload buffers still linked behind that fragment were freed as well, and the stale pointer was then reinstalled into the packet as buf->frags, producing a use-after-free and a later double free during packet teardown. The same loop also advanced to second->frags unconditionally: when the fragment still held payload after the header remainder was pulled, it was spliced out of the packet without ever being unreferenced, permanently leaking that buffer and silently dropping the data it carried.

The defect is reached from tcp_recv() via th_get() on every received TCP segment, before connection lookup or any header validation, so a single unauthenticated segment that matches a listening socket is sufficient. An attacker only needs the TCP header to straddle a net_buf boundary, which they can arrange from off-link: IPv6 extension headers are accepted on receive and their length is added to the header offset by th_get(), so a Destination Options header of a suitable length places the TCP header across the boundary of the fixed-size receive buffers (CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE). Packet chains assembled from several sources - IPv4/IPv6 reassembly, 6LoWPAN/802.15.4 reassembly, tunnel or virtual interfaces that strip an outer header, or drivers producing scatter-gather chains - can additionally present a short interior fragment that the loop empties exactly, which is the case that frees the remainder of the packet while it is still in use.

The reliably reachable consequence is exhaustion of the receive buffer pool: each crafted segment leaks one net_buf from the fixed CONFIG_NET_BUF_RX_COUNT pool, the buffers are never reclaimed, and once the pool is empty the device can no longer receive network traffic until it is rebooted. Where a fragment is emptied exactly, the impact rises to memory corruption: freed pool buffers are written through by the remainder of the loop, their contents may be delivered to the application, and the packet is double-freed on teardown.

The fix saves and clears second->frags before the net_buf_unref() so only the emptied header fragment is released, and advances to the next fragment only when second->len == 0, keeping any fragment that still holds payload in the packet. This restores the detach-before-unref ownership pattern used elsewhere in the stack, for example in net_pkt_trim_buffer().

title: The Dokan: AI Powered WooCommerce Multivendor Marketplace Solution – Build Your Own Amazon, eBay, Etsy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable...
summary: The Dokan: AI Powered WooCommerce Multivendor Marketplace Solution – Build Your Own Amazon, eBay, Etsy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.3. The vulnerability exists because the `matches_mcp_endpoint()` function applies an unanchored regular expression (`#/(?:woocommerce|dokan)/mcp(?:/|$)#`) against the entire `REQUEST_URI` including the query string, meaning any request that contains the literal substring `/dokan/mcp/` or `/woocommerce/mcp/` anywhere in its URI — including inside a query parameter value — is incorrectly treated as a trusted internal MCP context, causing `scope_product_permissions()` to unconditionally return `true` on WooCommerce's `woocommerce_rest_check_permissions` filter regardless of whether the caller is authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read full authenticated WooCommerce REST product records for any published product — including private underscore-prefixed meta, purchase notes, downloadable file URLs for paid digital products, catalog-hidden products, and edit-context representations — across the `/wc/v1`, `/wc/v2`, `/wc/v3`, and `/wc-analytics` REST namespaces. The bypass is triggered by appending a query parameter whose value contains the literal string `/dokan/mcp/` to any WooCommerce REST product endpoint (e.g., `/wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id}?x=/dokan/mcp/`); note that percent-encoding the slashes prevents the bypass, as the unencoded literal slash characters are required for the regex to match.

title: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server.
summary:

If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Version 0.10.0 never generates a root password, and the snapshot requires the manage_servers permission. If a 0.9.0 server generated its root password, change that password.

title: IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl let an on-path attacker choose the installed public suffix list because upd...
summary:
IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl let an on-path attacker choose the installed public suffix list because update_self_from_url fetches it over cleartext HTTP with no integrity check.

Called with no argument, as the module's documentation shows, the updater fetches the list from the `http://` address in the URL constant and checks only that the request succeeded, with no signature or digest over the response. The lines that come back are written into the module's own source file as the built-in list.

An attacker on the network path when the updater runs chooses the suffix boundary the module reports to every caller on the host, and that answer persists in the installed module until it is reinstalled. Dropping one rule makes the hostname check in IO::Socket::SSL accept a wildcard certificate that spans the whole public suffix that rule named.

title: Forge, also called node-forge, is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript.
summary: Forge, also called node-forge, is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.1, publicKey.verify() with the default RSASSA-PKCS1-V1_5 scheme in lib/rsa.js parses the recovered DigestInfo with the lenient BER parser asn1.fromDer() and validates its structure with digestInfoValidator without requiring canonical DER bytes. Non-minimal or indefinite lengths, malformed parameter values, and non-canonical object identifier encodings with padded subidentifiers or trailing bytes can leave attacker-controlled data inside an accepted DigestInfo. When the verifying RSA public key uses a low exponent such as e=3, an attacker can use that encoding slack to forge a signature without the private key. The same path is used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 signature verification. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.1.

title: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack.
summary: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 5.1.22, the @libp2p/crypto code reached by the default Identify service accepts a remote peer’s crafted publicKey before peer-id or signature verification and passes it through publicKeyFromProtobuf to the ASN.1 DER decoder. readLength in packages/crypto/src/keys/rsa/der.ts accepts long-form element lengths larger than the remaining buffer, causing readInteger and related readers to loop synchronously over an attacker-claimed length from a very small key blob. Because decoding occurs in one event-loop tick before the remotePeer equality check in packages/protocol-identify/src/identify.ts, the Identify timeout cannot interrupt it, allowing repeated unauthenticated connections to stall all timers and peers and transiently exhaust memory. This issue is fixed in version 5.1.22.

title: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack.
summary: libp2p is a JavaScript implementation of the libp2p networking stack. Prior to 17.0.0, the @libp2p/gossipsub default configuration allows a connected remote peer to submit unsigned subscription RPC metadata for arbitrarily many distinct topic strings. handleReceivedSubscription in packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts creates a persistent topics-map entry for each accepted topic, while allowedTopics is unset by default, decodeRpc maxSubscriptions limits only one RPC rather than aggregate topic bytes, and peer scoring has no subscription-volume penalty. A single peer can therefore grow the topics map and committed heap toward out-of-memory conditions, and disconnecting additionally causes removePeer to scan all accumulated topic entries. This issue is fixed in version 17.0.0.

title: ICRTouch PocketTouch version 1.700 build 2025.3726 transmits the POS socket password in plaintext XML over an unencrypted TCP connection.
summary:
ICRTouch PocketTouch version 1.700 build 2025.3726 transmits the POS socket password in plaintext XML over an unencrypted TCP connection. The protocol does not provide transport-layer encryption to protect credentials from interception.

An attacker able to observe network traffic between a PocketTouch device and a TouchPoint POS terminal can recover the socket password from captured packets.

title: The Vert.x HTTP client transport (a2a-java-sdk-http-client-vertx) hand-rolls a POST redirect follower that, when the documented PostBuild...

The sibling JDK and OkHttp/Android transports strip Authorization; Vert.x uniquely does not. This is a "fix introduced the bug" variant — the follower was added by the GHSA-9rhm hardening PR (3ae82912, refined by a5e76a0b).

An application that supplies a redirect-capable HttpClient (Redirect.NORMAL/ALWAYS) — which is the SDK-documented way to enable POST redirects — silently follows cross-authority redirects on every credentialed GET/DELETE request. The JDK strips Authorization cross-origin, but forwards the four allowlisted custom credential headers (X-API-Key, API-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-Authentication) to the attacker-controlled authority. This is an incomplete-fix variant of GHSA-9rhm: the fix hardened the default client and added a POST-only two-step opt-in, but never covered GET/DELETE.

title:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection i...
summary:
Issue summary: A QUIC server that rejects a stream opened by the peer may
retain that stream's state for the lifetime of the connection if the peer
resets the stream before the rejection is signalled, even though the peer's
stream credit is returned.

Impact summary: A remote client that completes a QUIC handshake can repeatedly
open and reset streams, causing server memory to grow without bound until the
process runs out of memory and every connection on it is lost. This is a
Denial of Service.

CWE: CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

Description: QUIC servers track each stream the peer opens. When the incoming
stream policy rejects a stream, OpenSSL schedules a STOP_SENDING frame, marks
the stream deleted and returns the peer's stream credit. A deleted stream is
collected only once its receive part is fully drained, which for a rejected
stream means the STOP_SENDING has been acknowledged. If the peer sends
RESET_STREAM first, the reset cancels the pending STOP_SENDING, so it is never
sent or acknowledged and the stream is never collected.

The default configuration reaches this path. Once a connection has a default
stream, meaning the application has read from or written to the connection as
the tutorial server does, the effective incoming stream policy rejects streams
the application does not accept. Applications that set the REJECT policy
explicitly are affected too.

Each retained stream costs about 300 bytes, and the peer's stream credit
window paces how quickly they accumulate. A client that keeps the connection
open and keeps opening and resetting streams grows server memory without
bound. The severity is Low because growth is slow, needs a long-lived
connection, and causes no memory corruption or disclosure.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

summary: mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 4.2.0 until 4.6.1, attacker-controlled email headers can cause polynomial regular-expression backtracking during ordinary parse_from_string(), parse_from_bytes(), or parse_from_file() calls. In src/mailparser/utils.py, get_addresses() invokes the _ADDR_FALLBACK_RE fallback when strict address parsing yields no usable address, and overlapping quantifiers rescan padded address headers quadratically or cubically. In src/mailparser/const.py, parse_received() applies _CLAUSE_SPLITTER to uncollapsed whitespace in a Received header, causing quadratic backtracking when a whitespace run is not followed by a clause keyword. title: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify.
summary: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, a multipart part whose header block is never terminated before the next boundary is counted by the vendored Dicer parser as an open part that never ends, so the parser emits neither a finish nor an error event and the request hangs. A single unauthenticated request of roughly one hundred bytes triggers the stall, and through @fastify/multipart the hung handler is not released when the client disconnects, so repeated requests leak handlers and whatever resources they hold, such as files, database connections and concurrency slots, until the process is restarted. The same parser is reached by the formData methods of undici versions 5.25.3 through 6.7.0. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, configure Fastify's handler timeout so hung handlers are eventually terminated and their resources released.

title: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify.
summary: @fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 1.0.0 through 3.2.5, when a request reaches the configured limit on the number of multipart parts, each further part is skipped without attaching an error listener to the skipped part stream. If the request body ends in the middle of such a skipped part, the vendored Dicer parser emits an error on that stream, and because nothing is listening Node.js raises an unhandled error event and the process exits. A single crafted unauthenticated request is therefore enough to crash the server. The bug is latent in the parser on its own and was first demonstrated through @fastify/multipart versions 10.1.2 through 10.1.4, which keep feeding the request body to the parser after a limit error, and it affects any consumer that sets a finite parts limit and parses request bodies that can be terminated early. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. There is no complete application level workaround because the crash happens inside the parser before application code runs, though consumers that set a finite parts limit should also attach an error listener to the parser stream.

title: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads.
summary: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 7.4.0 through 10.1.8, when the plugin is registered with the attachFieldsToBody option, the saveRequestFiles helper treats any object in the parsed request body that carries truthy file and buffer properties as an uploaded file. An unauthenticated client can forge such an object through a plain JSON request or a JSON-typed multipart field, so attacker-chosen bytes are written to the temporary directory while upload hooks and the file count and size limits are skipped, and the saved entry keeps the attacker's filename verbatim instead of being reduced to its basename. Because that filename can contain parent directory segments, applications that use it as a write destination, as the project README example does, are exposed to an arbitrary relative-path file write from a single request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.9, and users should upgrade to 10.1.9 or later. As a workaround, call saveRequestFiles only after confirming the request is multipart, and reduce each returned filename to its basename or validate it against an allowlist before using it as a destination.

title: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads.
summary: @fastify/multipart is the official Fastify plugin for handling multipart/form-data uploads. In versions 3.0.0 through 10.1.3, temporary files written by the saveRequestFiles helper are removed only by a response hook that runs when the response finishes or errors. When a client completes an upload and then disconnects before the handler writes the reply, for example while the handler scans, hashes or forwards the file, the response only emits a close event, the cleanup hook never runs, and the saved files are left on disk. An unauthenticated client can repeat this cheaply to exhaust disk space and deny service to applications that save uploaded files to disk. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.4, and users should upgrade to 10.1.4 or later. As a workaround, avoid saving request files for untrusted clients, or clean the saved files from a close handler on the raw response so removal also happens when the client disconnects.

title:

summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: stop processing a read response after a receive error

cifs_read_iter_from_socket() may call cifs_reconnect() before returning an
error.  The reconnect path aborts pending mids and invokes their callbacks.
The callback can then release the cifs_io_subrequest containing rdata.

cifs_readv_receive() nevertheless continues after a negative return and may
dereference rdata in cifs_readv_discard().  KASAN reports the resulting
UAF:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in cifs_readv_receive
  Read of size 4 by task cifsd
  cifs_readv_receive (fs/smb/client/transport.c:1284)
  cifs_demultiplex_thread (fs/smb/client/connect.c:1355)
  kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)
  ret_from_fork (arch/x86/kernel/process.c:158)

  Freed by task 148:
  netfs_put_subrequest (fs/netfs/objects.c:267)
  netfs_read_collection (fs/netfs/read_collect.c:460)
  netfs_wait_for_in_progress (fs/netfs/misc.c:462)

Return the socket error immediately, as this path did before the iterator
conversion.  This also avoids adding a negative length to total_read.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect

ksmbd_re...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix use-after-free after a failed durable reconnect

ksmbd_reopen_durable_fd() republishes a detached durable handle in the
reconnecting session's file table and takes no reference for that entry.
If smb2_open() then fails, cleanup relies on the final ksmbd_fd_put() to
remove the volatile id.

Two reconnects of the same handle can both take a lookup reference before
either attaches it. If the one that reopens first then fails and drops
its references first, the other request makes the final put through
ksmbd_put_durable_fd(). That frees the handle without removing the first
session's table entry, so tearing that session down writes to freed
memory.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
  Call Trace:
   __close_file_table_ids+0x14d/0x740 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_destroy_file_table+0x76/0x100 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_session_destroy+0xf8/0x480 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_dispose_sessions+0x13e/0x200 [ksmbd]
   ksmbd_conn_sessions_cleanup+0x4c3/0x6d0 [ksmbd]
  Freed by task 1030:
   __ksmbd_close_fd+0x97d/0x1000 [ksmbd]
   smb2_open+0x14eb/0xd9f0 [ksmbd]

Commit 3515503322f4 ("ksmbd: fix durable reconnect error path file
lifetime") handles a final put made by the reconnecting request, but not
one made by another holder.

Remove the volatile id under the file-table lock on this error path,
before the references are dropped, as ksmbd_close_fd() does on the
request_open path just above. Removal then no longer depends on which
holder makes the final put. The stale comment in the reconnect cleanup
is updated to match. A successful reconnect is unchanged.

title: Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" as...
summary: Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" assertion, so that a captured message cannot be accepted twice. It checked whether a value had already been seen, validated the message, and only then remembered the value, as two separate steps. If several copies of the same message were processed at the same time, they could all pass the check before any of them was remembered, and all be accepted. An attacker who obtained a valid message before the recipient first processed it could send several copies at once, so that the same authenticated request was executed more than once. Where a UsernameToken is not bound to the message by a signature, the copies could carry different message bodies. The attacker needs to obtain the message while it is still in transit; a message captured after it has been accepted cannot be replayed. Affects deployments with a replay cache configured, as Apache CXF has by default. The value is now checked and remembered in a single atomic step. Custom ReplayCache implementations should override the new ReplayCache.addIfAbsent method with an operation that is atomic in their underlying store. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.3 or 3.0.7 or 2.4.5, which fix this issue.

title: The MongoDB Java driver applies its DNS seedlist domain restriction to a record value that is later re-interpreted differently when the c...
summary: The MongoDB Java driver applies its DNS seedlist domain restriction to a record value that is later re-interpreted differently when the connection target is parsed, so the name that is checked and the name that is used can differ. An unauthenticated party who can set or forge the DNS service record for the seed domain in a connection string can cause the driver to direct its session to an unrelated host and to complete certificate verification against that host instead. This may result in unintended disclosure of application data and of configured database credentials, and in unintended content being returned to the application as query results.

title: An improper neutralization of delimiters in the MongoDB C# driver's DNS SRV connection-string resolution lets an unauthenticated party wh...
summary: An improper neutralization of delimiters in the MongoDB C# driver's DNS SRV connection-string resolution lets an unauthenticated party who can answer the client's DNS SRV query place a host outside the trusted domain into the client's server list. When an application resolves the connection string through the affected API and connects with the result, application data, authentication credentials and query results may pass through that host. This may result in unintended disclosure of data and credentials and in forged query results.

title: Poweradmin is a web-based DNS administration tool for PowerDNS server.
summary: Poweradmin is a web-based DNS administration tool for PowerDNS server. From 4.0.0 until 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1, lib/Domain/Service/MfaService.php verifies email second-factor codes through MfaService::verifyCode() without limiting failed attempts, and lib/Application/Controller/MfaVerifyController.php logs failures without throttling them. An attacker who knows the user's password can repeatedly guess the six-digit code during its ten-minute validity period when email MFA is enabled, potentially bypassing the second factor; the advisory notes MFA is disabled by default and that the practical request rate was not measured. This issue is fixed in versions 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1.

title: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify.
summary: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions 8.3.0 through 9.3.6, the internal helper that normalizes a path-scoped middleware's mount path only handles string inputs, but the use method also accepts an array of mount paths and passes it through unchanged, so the normalization silently does nothing. As a result, a trailing slash on an array element survives into the generated route-matching regular expression, and an element that is exactly the root path, meaning a catch-all mount, is dropped entirely. Requests to subroutes of the affected mount paths then skip the path-scoped middleware, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, while Fastify's router still dispatches them to the handler, allowing an unauthenticated client to reach protected routes. Applications are affected when they mount middleware on an array of paths in which an element ends with a slash, including one introduced by a plugin prefix that ends with a slash, or is exactly the root path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid array mount paths with a trailing slash element for security relevant middleware.

title: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify.
summary: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router's caseSensitive setting and matches path-scoped middleware mount paths with a case-insensitive regular expression that does not fold non-ASCII characters, while Fastify's router, when caseSensitive is set to false, lowercases the request path with a Unicode-aware conversion that maps the KELVIN SIGN character (U+212A) to the ASCII letter k. A request that spells a k in a protected mount path as the percent-encoded KELVIN SIGN is therefore routed to the protected handler while the middleware mounted on that path, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, never matches and is skipped, letting an unauthenticated client reach the handler. Only applications that set caseSensitive to false and protect a mount path containing the letter k are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, or keep routing case-sensitive, which is the default.

title: The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog.
summary: The Datadog Agent collects events and metrics from hosts and sends them to Datadog. Prior to datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0, the Datadog Single Step Instrumentation injector stores helper tooling in a predictable host directory. On Linux or Kubernetes systems with SSI enabled and at least one Java service instrumented through SSI, a local unprivileged attacker with shell access to the same host can influence that tooling and execute code with the privileges of the instrumented Java service. Services that use dd-java-agent without SSI and non-Java language runtimes are not affected. This issue is fixed in datadog-apm-inject 0.66.0.

title: The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and inclu...
summary: The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.1 via the '_cf7mls_db_form_data_id' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to permanently delete arbitrary stored Contact Form 7 submissions from the database. Exploitation requires the companion CF7 Database plugin to be active and the per-form "Save every step, not just the final submission" option to be enabled.

title: The Bizuno Accounting – ERP/Accounting/CRM (for WordPress) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Password Reset...
summary: The Bizuno Accounting – ERP/Accounting/CRM (for WordPress) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Password Reset Token Disclosure in all versions up to, and including, 7.4.5 via the `bizUser` parameter of the `validateReset()` function on the `portal/api/lostPW` endpoint. This is due to `portalCtl::goAPI()` failing to call `loadBusinessCache()` before invoking the handler, which causes `isMailConfigured()` to read an empty business cache and return false regardless of the site's actual mail configuration, causing the fully-qualified reset URL — containing the victim's live reset UUID and numeric user ID — to be embedded directly in the HTML response rather than delivered by email. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain a valid password-reset token for any Bizuno account, including administrators, directly from the HTTP response and submit it to the `portal/api/lostVal` endpoint to rewrite the victim's password and achieve full account takeover. The administrator email address required to initiate the reset is frequently exposed by the plugin's own login error messages and the public `/bizuno/` portal page, making exploitation trivial against most installations.

title: An incorrect authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated user whose numeric user...
summary: An incorrect authorization vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated user whose numeric user ID matched an enterprise's numeric ID to manage that enterprise's GitHub Apps and generate private keys without enterprise membership. GitHub App ownership checks compared numeric IDs without checking the owner's account type. Exploitation required control of a session for the colliding user account and an enterprise-owned GitHub App. A generated private key could be used to authenticate as the App and access repositories where it was installed, within its granted permissions. On standard fresh installations, the documented collision involved the non-loginable built-in ghost account; the reported GHES reproduction used site administrator impersonation. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.19.16, 3.20.12, 3.21.10, and 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

title: A command injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated site administrator to execute ...
summary: A command injection vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed an authenticated site administrator to execute arbitrary commands as the host git user on peer Git server nodes outside the pre-receive hook sandbox by supplying a crafted pre-receive environment download URL. Exploitation required a clustered deployment using custom pre-receive hook environments and at least one peer Git server node. This vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.23 and was fixed in versions 3.22.5, 3.21.10, 3.20.12, and 3.19.16. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

title: Snap7 through 1.4.3 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in TSnap7MicroClient::opReadSZL() that allows malicious PLCs to overwrite clien...
summary: Snap7 through 1.4.3 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in TSnap7MicroClient::opReadSZL() that allows malicious PLCs to overwrite client memory by sending oversized multi-slice SZL responses. A rogue or impersonated PLC can keep flagging more data with attacker-controlled DLen slices, overflowing the 65536-byte opData buffer via Cli_ReadSZL() and Cli_ReadSZLList(), crashing the client and corrupting heap memory.

title: Snap7 through 1.4.3 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in TSnap7MicroClient::opReadMultiVars() that allows malicious PLCs to o...
summary: Snap7 through 1.4.3 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in TSnap7MicroClient::opReadMultiVars() that allows malicious PLCs to overflow client buffers via unchecked DataLength fields. Attackers controlling or impersonating a PLC can return crafted ReadVar responses to Cli_ReadMultiVars() callers, writing up to 65535 bytes per item to corrupt memory and crash clients.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with access to the configured load balancer account could replace a load balancer helper that...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with access to the configured load balancer account could replace a load balancer helper that Splunk SOAR later runs with root privileges during cluster lifecycle operations. If a Splunk SOAR administrator performs a cluster lifecycle operation, Splunk SOAR could execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the load balancer.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify the integrity or ownership of the load balancer helper before running it with root privileges.

title: In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-control...
summary:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in Updates data. If another user who can access the System Update Status report selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the System Update Status report does not validate destination, signature, and vendor-product values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and System Update Status (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/system-update-status) in the Splunk documentation.

title: In Splunk App for Payment Card Industry Compliance versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_user" Splunk Enterprise Security role ...
summary:
In Splunk App for Payment Card Industry Compliance versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_user" Splunk Enterprise Security role could add attacker-controlled values to lookup data used by the Primary Functions report. If another authenticated user later selects the value in the Primary Function Summary panel, the Splunk App for Payment Card Industry Compliance could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selected the value. With this access, the first user could expose or modify data available to the user who selected the value.
The vulnerability is possible because the Primary Functions report does not safely escape report values before including them in drilldown searches.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Reports (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/user-manual/8.7/using-the-splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/reports) in the Splunk documentation.

title: A caller who can send requests to the temporal-proxy gRPC listener can obtain the static API key of an upstream whose address is template...
summary: A caller who can send requests to the temporal-proxy gRPC listener can obtain the static API key of an upstream whose address is templated from the request namespace, and then use that key directly against the upstream Temporal service. temporal-proxy does not validate the request namespace before rendering it into a templated upstream address, so when an upstream's hostPort is templated from the namespace, as in the published Temporal Cloud configuration example, a crafted namespace changes the host the proxy dials. If that upstream verifies TLS against the system trust store and sets no literal server name, a caller-controlled host with a publicly trusted certificate passes verification and receives the key. The built-in static-token and JWKS authenticators do not restrict namespaces, so any caller they admit can do this; an external authenticator that admits only listed namespaces prevents it. temporal-proxy versions 0.1.0 through 1.2.0 are affected. The issue is fixed in 1.0.2, 1.1.2, and 1.2.1, and releases before 1.0.0 receive no fix. Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed minor release line, and rotate any upstream API key that untrusted callers could reach.

Upgrading to version 1.8.7 will fix this issue. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could use the Automation Dependenc...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could use the Automation Dependency Wheel Representational State Transfer (REST) API to write arbitrary files outside the intended directory, which could lead to arbitrary code execution.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not restrict uploaded automation dependency wheel filenames to the intended storage directory.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could use a customer automation de...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could use a customer automation dependency to execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not properly separate customer automation dependencies from trusted product code.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could execute arbit...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could execute arbitrary code on the host that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API accepts package references from untrusted sources and passes them to the dependency installer.

title: In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission and restricted tenant access could...
summary:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission and restricted tenant access could modify settings for a tenant outside the role scope through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. With this access, the user could expose confidential tenant environment values, alter tenant settings and automation behavior, or take the tenant out of operation.
The vulnerability is possible because the Tenant REST API checks the System Settings edit permission but does not enforce the tenant restrictions for the role before it updates the selected tenant.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), Configure multiple tenants on your Splunk SOAR (On-premises) instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/configure-multiple-tenants-on-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance), and REST Tenant (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/8.5.0/multi-tenancy-endpoints/rest-tenant) in the Splunk documentation.

title: The WP-Slimbox2 Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up t...
summary: The WP-Slimbox2 Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a logged-in user, typically an administrator, to click the attacker's image link in the comment; however, because unmoderated comments appear in the WordPress moderation queue where administrators routinely interact with them, the moderation gate does not meaningfully prevent exploitation. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

title: The Slimbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (anchor title within comment HTML)' parame...
summary: The Slimbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (anchor title within comment HTML)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core comment KSES permits unauthenticated commenters to post anchor elements with href and title attributes, so an entity-encoded payload stored in the title attribute survives sanitization verbatim; the browser then decodes the entities when populating the DOM .title property, and the Slimbox library's jQuery .html() caption sink renders it as executable HTML.

title: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms.
summary: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms allows a user with repository management privileges to inject shell syntax through repository uri, branch, name, or host values processed by server/src/models/repo.model.js. The Repo.clone and Repo.addKnownHosts paths interpolate these values into git and ssh-keyscan command strings, and server/src/lib/cmd.js executes the strings through Cmd.executeSilentCommand with shell interpretation enabled. Creating or updating a repository can therefore execute arbitrary commands as the AnsibleForms application process. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.1.

title: The WP Instant Feeds plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[images][][url]' parameter in all ver...
summary: The WP Instant Feeds plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[images][][url]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. title: The WEB-Translation – eTranslation Multilingual plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' param...
summary: The WEB-Translation – eTranslation Multilingual plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires that at least one secondary language is configured in the plugin and that comments are open on the target post; because the stored payload contains no literal HTML brackets at save-time, WordPress core KSES filtering does not remove it, and the malicious script is only materialized when a visitor loads the post under a secondary-language URL slug.

The injected script is stored via the advcb_live_activity transient on the init hook and executed when an administrator views the Live Monitor page, as the stored URI is unsafely concatenated into a double-quoted HTML title attribute and inserted into the DOM via jQuery .html().

title: The AMP for WP – Accelerated Mobile Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and includ...
summary: The AMP for WP – Accelerated Mobile Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.19 via comment content rendered on AMP post pages. The plugin registers an output-buffer callback ampforwp_the_content_filter_full() on the 'wp' action (priority 999) that applies a set of tag-agnostic and quote-agnostic regular expressions — notably /onclick=[^>]*/ — to the entire AMP page output after approved comments have already been echoed into it; these regexes do not understand HTML tag or attribute-value boundaries, so a kses-legal comment that places strings like 'onclick="' inside a title attribute value can trigger deletion of the title's closing quote, causing the browser to re-parse what was previously textual content inside the attribute value as live HTML attributes. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page, after an administrator has approved the comment.

title: The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' merge-tag of the [ghr] shortcode in...
summary: The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' merge-tag of the [ghr] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 4.10 The post_title replacement is registered with 'nested' => true, so the nested branch of Replacements::do_replacement() returns the merge value through tackle_replacements() without passing it through escape_merge_tags()/escape_shortcodes(); the callback single_post() calls html_entity_decode(get_the_title(), ENT_QUOTES), converting the entity-encoded text that wp_filter_kses leaves intact on a Contributor's post title back into raw HTML, which is then emitted into the rendered post. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

title: Vulnerability in the Oracle Access Manager product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Authentication Engine).
summary: Vulnerability in the Oracle Access Manager product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Authentication Engine).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.1.0. While the vulnerability is in Oracle Access Manager, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Access Manager accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Access Manager accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.2 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N).

title: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions.
summary: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.9.1, a user with backup-management permission can upload a crafted gzip-compressed tar archive through web/html/configuracao/importar_dump.php, after which web/controle/control.php accepts a user-controlled modulo value and combines it with nomeClasse for require_once(). By using a phar:// path to the uploaded archive and selecting the whitelisted InternoControle, whose empty resource list is treated as authorized, the user can cause an embedded controller file and its requested method to execute as the web-server process. The attack path depends on the configured BKP_DIR, and enabling phar.readonly or phar.require_hash does not prevent PHP from reading the gzip tar archive through phar://. Successful exploitation permits access to or modification of sensitive data, configuration, credentials, source files, host commands, and services reachable by the web-server account. This issue is fixed in version 3.9.1.

title: Vulnerability in the Product Lifecycle Analytics product of Oracle Supply Chain (component: Installation Issues).
summary: Vulnerability in the Product Lifecycle Analytics product of Oracle Supply Chain (component: Installation Issues).   The supported version that is affected is 3.6.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Product Lifecycle Analytics executes to compromise Product Lifecycle Analytics. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Product Lifecycle Analytics accessible data as well as  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Product Lifecycle Analytics accessible data. title: Ikaros is a content management system for ACGMN media.
summary: Ikaros is a content management system for ACGMN media. Prior to 1.2.0, server/src/main/java/run/ikaros/server/core/tag/TagEndpoint.java does not enforce tag ownership for authenticated users with tag permissions. GET /tags/condition accepts an arbitrary userId and can enumerate another user's tags, DELETE /tag/id/{id} deletes a tag without comparing its owner to the requester, and DELETE /tag/condition omits userId from its filter and can delete every user's tags matching the supplied condition. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.0.

title: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker.
summary: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.6.2 until 6.7, PATCH /api/config accepts unfiltered CivetWeb lua_* options through webserver.advancedOpts, while POST /api/teleporter writes attacker-controlled content from a dhcp.leases archive entry through src/zip/teleporter.c without content validation. An authenticated administrator can place controlled file content on disk, point a Lua execution option at that file, and rely on the advancedOpts configuration change to restart FTL. CivetWeb then executes the file as Lua through the processing in src/webserver/webserver.c, allowing arbitrary commands to run as the pihole operating-system user and persist across restarts while the configuration and file remain. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

title: In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, an unauthenticated user could craft a malicious link that, if op...

title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, fai_retrieve does not verify that the line width recorded in a FASTA .fai index is greater than or equal to the number of bases per line. When the line width is exactly one less than the base count, retrieval allocates an undersized heap buffer and writes one byte beyond its end; larger discrepancies instead cause an allocation failure that is handled. This issue can corrupt heap memory and crash the process. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

title: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats.
summary: HTSlib is a library for reading and writing bioinformatics file formats. Prior to 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24, cram_index_load does not verify that the number of reference sequences in a CRAM .crai index does not exceed the CRAM header reference count. A malformed index can drive unbounded index-array allocation, and when the number of references in the index is within two of INT_MAX, the growth calculation can wrap, read beyond a heap buffer, and use the resulting value as a pointer for an unchecked memory write. Any region query can trigger the flaw, causing denial of service or memory corruption. This issue is fixed in versions 1.21.2, 1.22.3, 1.23.2, and 1.24.

title: NATS Server: MQTT SUBSCRIBE Protocol Injection via Leaf Node/Route Forwarding allows arbitrary NATS command injection

title: MRemoteNG establishes encrypted but unauthenticated channel with Microsoft SQL Server backend.
summary:
MRemoteNG establishes encrypted but unauthenticated channel with Microsoft SQL Server backend. Client accepts any certificate the server
presents, including a self-signed certificate supplied by an attacker. An attacker positioned between the client and the SQL server (for example via ARP/DNS spoofing) can
transparently pintercept the connection (man-in-the-middle) and read all traffic, including the encrypted connection-password table read and the database login.




Vendor did not provide the range of vulnerable versions. Only version 1.76.20 was tested and confirmed vulnerable. Other versions may also be vulnerable.

title: In Eclipse Ditto versions before 3.9.9, Thing events delivered via WebSocket, Server-Sent Events and connections disclose field values wh...
summary:
In Eclipse Ditto versions before 3.9.9, Thing events delivered via WebSocket, Server-Sent Events and connections disclose field values which the policy does not allow the subscriber to read. A READ

  revoke for one subject of the subscriber's authorization context is not applied when another of its subjects is granted READ. For subscribers with partial READ access, subscription RQL filters, the SSE
  `_context`, `thing-json` placeholders and extra fields are evaluated on the unfiltered event. This allows an authenticated subscriber with at least partial READ access to a Thing to obtain the values of
  fields it may not read when events for that Thing are emitted.

title: In Eclipse Ditto versions 2.4.0 to 3.9.8, Thing fields a requester is not allowed to read can be disclosed through the `condition` and `l...
summary:
In Eclipse Ditto versions 2.4.0 to 3.9.8, Thing fields a requester is not allowed to read can be disclosed through the `condition` and `live-channel-condition` headers, which are evaluated against the

  full Thing: the READ check of `live-channel-condition` is skipped when a `condition` header is also present on Thing query commands (3.0.0 to 3.9.8); both headers are evaluated without any authorization
  on WoT Thing Description requests (`Accept: application/td+json`) when WoT TD permission filtering is not active (by default in 3.0.0 to 3.8.14, in 2.4.x with WoT integration enabled, and in 3.9.x with
  filtering disabled); the `condition` of live messages and live events is evaluated without a READ check, and of claim messages without any permission (3.1.0 to 3.9.8); and the twin response of a Thing
  query with a non-matching `live-channel-condition` is returned without filtering it by the policy (3.0.0 to 3.9.8). This allows an authenticated user to read Thing fields they are not allowed to read, in
  some cases without any permission on the Thing.

title: In Eclipse Ditto versions 2.0.0 to 3.8.14 and 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the authorization check for JSON merge patch commands on Things (HTTP `PATC...
summary:
In Eclipse Ditto versions 2.0.0 to 3.8.14 and 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the authorization check for JSON merge patch commands on Things (HTTP `PATCH` / Ditto Protocol `merge`) does not check permissions for fields

  deleted or set to an empty object by the patch: fields with a `null` value or an empty object value (`{}`) are skipped by the check, and Ditto's regex-based key deletion with the documented `{{
  ~<regex>~ }}` syntax is not recognized as a deletion. An authenticated user with WRITE permission on any part of a Thing can therefore delete other attributes, features and the definition of that Thing,
  or overwrite or create fields as empty objects, including parts the policy revokes or never grants WRITE on.

title: A flaw was found in OpenSCAP.
summary: A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. This vulnerability allows for information disclosure when performing offline scans of untrusted filesystem images, such as container images or virtual machine (VM) disks. Because the scanner does not properly restrict symbolic link (symlink) resolution to the target image's root directory, an attacker can supply a crafted image containing links pointing to files on the host system. When the scan runs, typically with elevated privileges, OpenSCAP follows these links to read sensitive host files and expose their contents in the scan report or manipulate compliance results.

summary: ### Summary `keystore.Decode()` fails to check the error returned when reading the trailing SHA-1 integrity digest of a JKS keystore. title: A caller with write permission in a namespace can terminate temporal-proxy through memory exhaustion by storing highly compressed payload...
summary: A caller with write permission in a namespace can terminate temporal-proxy through memory exhaustion by storing highly compressed payloads in Workflow history, and the stored history causes the same failure on every later read. temporal-proxy 1.2.0 decompresses every payload marked as compressed in the responses it forwards, whether or not compression is configured. Each payload is limited to 4 MiB after decompression, but the total for a response is not, and the decoded payloads are held in memory together. The caller can store many small, highly compressed payloads through the proxy or directly at the upstream Temporal service. When that history is read through the proxy, for example by a Worker processing a task, the proxy can run out of memory and be terminated. The codec server's /decode endpoint is affected in the same way when it is enabled. Only temporal-proxy 1.2.0 is affected; earlier versions do not decompress payloads. The issue is fixed in 1.2.1. Upgrade to 1.2.1 or later.

summary: A Session Fixation vulnerability exists in the admin login endpoint (/admin/index.php) of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1. The application fails to regenerate the session identifier (PHPSESSID) upon successful authentication. A remote attacker can exploit this by setting a known session ID in the victim's browser prior to login. title: WarehousePG (WHPG) 6.27.1 through 6.27.7 and 7.2.1 through 7.6.1 are affected by an out-of-bounds write vulnerability (CWE-787) in gpfdis...
summary: WarehousePG (WHPG) 6.27.1 through 6.27.7 and 7.2.1 through 7.6.1 are affected by an out-of-bounds write vulnerability (CWE-787) in gpfdist, the file server used to load and unload external tables. When gpfdist attaches a request to a session, it sizes two internal arrays from the client-supplied X-GP-SEGMENT-COUNT header and writes to them at the index given by the X-GP-SEGMENT-ID header, without checking that the index is non-negative and smaller than the count (CWE-129). gpfdist does not authenticate callers unless gpfdists is used with client certificate verification, so an attacker who can reach the gpfdist port can crash it with a single HTTP request, failing every external table load or unload that uses that gpfdist instance. gpfdist is normally reachable only from the cluster's internal network.

title: An authorization bypass through user-controlled key vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed authenticated u...
summary: An authorization bypass through user-controlled key vulnerability was identified in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed authenticated users to read review-thread data from private repositories they could not access. An attacker required an authenticated account, a readable repository and pull request to use as the request context, and target review-thread identifiers. The thread-preview endpoint resolved supplied identifiers without restricting them to the authorized pull request, exposing private file paths and, when positioning and diff data were available, source-code excerpts, commit identifiers, and line metadata without victim interaction. This vulnerability affected supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases in the 3.21, 3.22 series and was fixed in versions 3.21.10, 3.22.5. This vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.

title: Incorrect authorization in the credential handling for namespace-scoped issuers in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca...
summary:
Incorrect authorization in the credential handling for namespace-scoped issuers in AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes (aws-privateca-issuer) before 1.12.0 might allow an authenticated remote user with permission to create namespace-scoped issuers to obtain certificates, including subordinate CA certificates, from every AWS Private CA and certificate template reachable by the controller's own AWS identity or by any IAM role that identity can assume. This happens because a namespace-scoped issuer that supplies no credentials, or sets only a role, falls back to the controller's own identity.



To remediate this issue, users should first update any namespace-scoped issuers that rely on the controller's identity to use their own credentials. Then, upgrade aws-privateca-issuer to version 1.12.0 or the AWS Private CA Connector for Kubernetes EKS add-on to version v1.12.0-eksbuild.1.

title: ESP-IDF is the Espressif Internet of Things (IoT) Development Framework.
summary: ESP-IDF is the Espressif Internet of Things (IoT) Development Framework. Prior to 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3, the Bluedroid BLE Mesh GATT server read handler bt_mesh_bta_gatts_cb in esp_ble_mesh stores a signed attribute-read callback length in an unsigned 16-bit variable. A negative ATT error code is therefore interpreted as a very large successful length and used for a memory copy from a small stack buffer into the GATT response structure. A remote attacker within Bluetooth LE range who can connect to an exposed PB-GATT provisioning or Mesh Proxy service can trigger a failed attribute read with a crafted request. On devices where the affected attributes are accessible without pairing, exploitation requires neither pairing nor user interaction; access requirements depend on device configuration. The resulting out-of-bounds read and stack-based buffer overflow corrupts the Bluetooth host task stack, causing a crash and device restart and potentially further memory corruption. The issue affects devices built with CONFIG_BT_BLUEDROID_ENABLED=y and BLE Mesh GATT enabled; the NimBLE host path is not affected. This issue is fixed in versions 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.5.6, and 6.0.3.

summary:

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

libceph: bound mon_command ack decode to front len

handle_command_a...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

libceph: bound mon_command ack decode to front len

handle_command_ack() bounds the decode with msg->front_alloc_len, the size
of the reply buffer, instead of msg->front.iov_len, the number of bytes the
monitor sent.  mon_alloc_msg() routes every CEPH_MSG_MON_COMMAND_ACK to
get_generic_reply(), which returns the preallocated ->reply of whichever
generic request carries the same tid, so the buffer keeps its fixed size
however short the reply is.  An ack with hdr.front_len below sizeof(struct
ceph_mon_request_header) + sizeof(u32), including 0, still passes
ceph_decode_need(), and ceph_decode_32() returns four bytes that were never
received: uninitialized slab memory, stale bytes of an earlier message, or
bytes the peer planted by sending a reply that lands in the same buffer and
is then rejected.  The read stays within the allocation, so KASAN does not
flag it.

req->result reaches userspace through ceph_monc_do_statfs(),
ceph_monc_get_version() and ceph_monc_blocklist_add(); rbd hands it back
from write() on /sys/bus/rbd/add_single_major, and rbd_get_client() passes
it to ERR_PTR() unchecked, which faults:

  rbd: failed to get latest osdmap: -186318427
  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfffe9ca034
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  RIP: 0010:do_rbd_add (drivers/block/rbd.c:7105)
  Call Trace:
   ...
   kernfs_fop_write_iter (fs/kernfs/file.c:345)
   vfs_write (fs/read_write.c:595 fs/read_write.c:687)
   ksys_write (fs/read_write.c:739)
   do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:61 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:84)
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121)
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Use msg->front.iov_len, matching handle_subscribe_ack(),
handle_statfs_reply(), handle_get_version_reply() and handle_auth_reply().
A well-formed ack has front.iov_len >= 22 and is unaffected; a short one
takes the existing bad: path.  This applies commit d3c32939fa0e ("libceph:
bound get_version reply decode to front len") to the last decode-side
use of front_alloc_len in this file.

ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()

rawv6_send_hdr...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()

rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to
l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release
the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale.

The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting
and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Its RCU read-side critical
section starts after l3mdev_ip6_out(), so it cannot prevent the old route
from being reclaimed in between.

Reload the route from the current skb destination after
l3mdev_ip6_out() returns.

KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route
allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and
the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().

title: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system.
summary: Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line and in 2.0.0, plugin/cleandeletedfiles/src/ajax.php and public/plugin/CleanDeletedFiles/src/ajax.php pass the request path parameter and list parameter directly to unlink without canonicalization, filename validation, or confinement to the plugin's scanned directories. An authenticated administrator can delete arbitrary files writable by the web server; a cross-site request forgery against an administrator session can reach the same operation. Deleting application source, uploaded content, cache, or configuration files can cause data loss and denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.40 on the 1.11 release line. No fixed 2.0 release is established as of this review.

title:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams

usb_str...
summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams

usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and
only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb,
sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs
of each direction.

A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so
the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run
before those pointers are set.  While the stream is still being
synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls
playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still
NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7]
  RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596
   i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654
   __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657
   usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691
   tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994
   handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645
   </IRQ>

The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and
do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit
loop.  Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a
well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills
and resubmits the streams.

title: llama.cpp MTMD Multimodal GGUF File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability.
summary:
llama.cpp MTMD Multimodal GGUF File Parsing Integer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of llama.cpp. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of audio multimodal projector GGUF files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in an integer overflow before allocating a buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-30980.

A second sink embeds unvalidated popup geometry (`-x/-y/-w/-h/-p`) into an unquoted `tmux popup ... $opt ...` invocation, allowing injection of tmux flags such as `-e BASH_ENV=<path>` (command execution via non-interactive bash sourcing `$BASH_ENV`). ### Reporter /

title: Bludit is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the page deletion functionality.
summary:
Bludit is vulnerable to Path Traversal in the page deletion functionality. An authenticated user with the Author role can set the UUID field of their own page to contain path traversal sequences (.. and path separators), which are saved without proper validation. When the page is deleted, Pages::delete() passes the path constructed from this UUID to Filesystem::deleteRecursive() without verifying that it still points to an allowed directory, allowing the attacker to delete any files, even not belonging to them. Critically, it is possible to delete admin pages and render the site unusable.


Because vendor contact attempts were unsuccessful, the vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.22.0 but may also affect other versions.

summary:
In
the Matter and Aliro Door Lock Application of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door
Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1 with
CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE enabled, deleting a Credential Issuer passes the
1-based Matter credential index to ClearValidityIterations(), which expects a
0-based storage index. The intended issuer's ValidityIteration state is left in
place, and the state of the adjacent, still-provisioned issuer is cleared. This
resets that issuer's rollback protection. An attacker holding an older but correctly
signed Access Document from the adjacent issuer, whose validity iteration had
been superseded, can then potentially obtain physical access. Fixed in v1.2.0.

summary:
In the Aliro access control reference
  applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control
  Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, the stored Access Document record does not
  retain validFrom and validUntil. The cached public key path (VerifyPublicKey())
  and the Kpersistent fast path (_VerifyKPersistentKey()) therefore never
  re-evaluate the Access Document validity period. An attacker who held a
  time-limited Aliro credential that was valid when first presented can
  continue to obtain physical access after the Access Document has expired, for
  as long as the cached record remains available. Fixed in v1.2.0.

title: containerd image-triggered daemon crash via malformed digest in subject-annotated descriptor
summary: ### Impact A bug in containerd's image manifest processing causes an unrecovered panic when a child descriptor contains the `io.containerd.manifest.subject` annotation and a malformed digest. Pulling or importing such an image through the transfer service (including default CRI `PullImage` requests) crashes the containerd daemon. In Kubernetes environments, `kubelet` retries failed image pulls with backoff, allowing a pod referencing an untrusted image to repeatedly crash containerd and disrupt container operations on the worker node. ### Patches This bug has been fixed in containerd 2.4.2, 2.

title: @nuxt/webpack-builder and @nuxt/rspack-builder dev server serves built source to DNS rebinding pages
summary: ### Summary When using the webpack or rspack builder, the dev server serves built client chunks to any request whose `Host` header matches its `Origin`/`Referer`, or that carries `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`.
